ASAD-NOTES:14:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:intro/r1.claim: All authorities place the surah among the late Meccan revelations; Asad accepts the Itqan's placement immediately after surah 71, and its title comes from Abraham's prayer.
ASAD-NOTES:14:intro/r1.anchor: ALL AUTHORITIES agree that this surah belongs to the last group of Meccan revelations

ASAD-NOTES:14:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:intro/r2.claim: The surah presents revelation in each people's language to lead them from darkness to light, while earlier scripture addressed its own people and the Qur'an addresses all humanity.
ASAD-NOTES:14:intro/r2.anchor: the Qur'an is, as stated in the first and the last verses of this surah, a message for all mankind

STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r1.claim: Sūrah Ibrāhīm is the fifth of six sūrahs beginning with alif, lām, rāʾ and speaking of the Book.
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r1.anchor: verses include the letters alif, lām, and rāʾ, and which speak of

STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r2.speaker: My
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r2.claim: It is said to be Makkan except verses 28–29, which are Madinan and usually understood to refer to Badr.
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r2.anchor: which belong to the Madinan period, as these two verses are usually considered to refer to the Battle of Badr (My)

STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r5.claim: A key theme is the sharp difference between gratitude and ingratitude for God’s blessings.
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r5.anchor: gratitude and ingratitude for God’s Blessings (see vv. 5, 7–8, 28, 32–34, 37)

STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r13.claim: Prophecy guides people out of darkness into light.
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r13.anchor: prophecy as a means of guiding people out of darkness into light (vv. 1, 5)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Prophet's task is to deliver the message; God determines who accepts faith and gives each person what they deserve.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: his responsibility is to only deliver the message.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p230/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p230/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p230/r2.claim: In the mystical allusion, the revealed Book brings people from multiplicity to unity, from the qualities of embodied nature to primordial nature, or from veils of acts and attributes to the pure light of the divine essence.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p230/r2.anchor: فقيل : من ظلمات الكثرة إلى نور الوحدة أو من ظلمات صفات النشأة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p230/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p230/r3.speaker: جعفر
ALUSI-FULL:v13p230/r3.claim: Jaʿfar interprets the darknesses as disbelief, innovation, and the self, and the light as faith, the Sunna, and the heart.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p230/r3.anchor: وقال جعفر : من ظلمات الكفر إلى نور الايمان ومن ظلمات البدعة إلى نور السنة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p230/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p230/r4.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
ALUSI-FULL:v13p230/r4.claim: Abū Bakr ibn Ṭāhir reads the movement as from the darkness of conjecture to the light of reality.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p230/r4.anchor: وقال أبو بكر بن طاهر : من ظلمات الظن إلى نور الحقيقة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p230/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p230/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p230/r5.claim: God's permission means enabling the movement by giving readiness and preparing the causes that bring latent capacity into action.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p230/r5.anchor: ( باذن ربهم ) بتيسيره بهبة الاستعداد وتهيئة أسباب الخروج إلى الفعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p404#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p404#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p404#2/r1.claim: The majority says the whole surah is Meccan; Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda exempt the passage about those who exchanged God’s favor for disbelief through the verse about entering the Fire.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p404#2/r1.anchor: هذه السورة مكية كلها في قول الجمهور، وعن ابن عباس وقتادة، هي مكية إلا من قوله: ألم تر إلى الذين بدلوا نعمت الله كفرا الآية إلى قوله إلى النار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p404#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p404#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p404#2/r2.claim: The opening connects clearly to Sūrat al-Raʿd, which ended with references to a Qur’an, its Arabic judgment, and the witness possessing knowledge of the Book.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p404#2/r2.anchor: ارتباط أول هذه السورة بالسورة قبلها واضح جدا، لأنه ذكر فيها: ولو أن قرآنا ثم وكذلك أنزلناه حكما عربيا ثم ومن عنده علم الكتاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p404#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p404#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p404#2/r3.claim: After the request for a sign and the statement that God guides whom He wills, the revealed Book is presented as a sufficient sign that leads people from error to guidance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p404#2/r3.anchor: لولا أنزل عليه آية من ربه وقيل له: قل إن الله يضل من يشاء ويهدي إليه من أناب أنزل الر كتاب أنزلناه إليك كأنه قيل: أو لم يكفهم من الآيات كتاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r1.claim: الر can be nominative as a subject with كتاب as predicate, nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject, or accusative under an implied command to recite or keep to it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r1.anchor: أن يكون في موضع رفع بالابتداء، وكتاب الخبر، أو في موضع رفع على خبر مبتدأ محذوف تقديره: هذه الر، وفي موضع نصب على تقدير: الزم أو اقرأ الر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r2.claim: كتاب may be a subject because an understood adjective such as great qualifies it, or a predicate for an omitted “this is”; أنزلناه may then be its adjective.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r2.anchor: وكتاب مبتدأ. وسوغ الابتداء به كونه موصوفا في التقدير أي: كتاب أي: عظيم أنزلناه إليك.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r3.claim: The plural “We sent it down,” direct address to the Prophet, and assigning him the task of leading people out honor him as a participant in guidance, though God originates it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r3.anchor: وإسناد الإنزال إلى نون العظمة ومخاطبته تعالى بقوله إليك، وإسناد الإخراج إليه عليه الصلاة والسلام، تنويه عظيم وتشريف له

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r4.claim: الناس means humanity generally because the Prophet was sent to all creation; darkness and light metaphorically mean unbelief and faith.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r4.anchor: والناس عام، إذ هو مبعوث إلى الخلق كلهم، والظلمات والنور مستعاران للكفر والإيمان.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r5.claim: بإذن ربهم means the leading out occurs through the Master’s facilitation and care for His servants; calling Him رب highlights His beneficence and stewardship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r5.anchor: ذلك الإخراج بتسهيل مالكهم الناظر في مصالحهم، إذ هم عبيده، فناسب ذكر الرب هنا تنبيها على منة المالك،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r6.claim: The apparent syntax attaches بإذن to لتخرج; Abū al-Baqāʾ also permits treating it as a circumstantial phrase meaning the Prophet is authorized.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r6.anchor: وبإذن ظاهره التعلق بقوله: لتخرج. وجوز أبو البقاء أن يكون بإذن ربهم في موضع الحال قال: أي مأذونا لك.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains “by their Lord’s permission” as facilitation and ease, metaphorically borrowing permission’s sense of opening a barrier and referring to divine grace and guidance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r7.anchor: بإذن ربهم بتسهيله وتيسيره، مستعار من الإذن الذي هو تسهيل الحجاب، وذلك ما يمنحهم من اللطف والتوفيق انتهى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p405/r8.claim: Abū Ḥayyān detects a Muʿtazilite implication in al-Zamakhsharī’s explanation of divine permission.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p406/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p406/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p406/r1.claim: The phrase “to a path” is apposition to “to the light”; the intervening phrase causes no problem because “by permission” is governed by the verb attached to “to the light.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p406/r1.anchor: الظاهر أن قوله: إلى صراط، بدل من قوله إلى النور، ولا يضر هذا الفصل بين المبدل منه والبدل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p406/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p406/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p406/r2.claim: He allows “to a path” to begin a new sentence answering the implied question, “to what light?”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p406/r2.anchor: وأجاز الزمخشري أن يكون إلى صراط على وجه الاستئناف، كأنه قيل: إلى أي نور، فقيل: إلى صراط العزيز الحميد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p406/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p406/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p406/r3.claim: A reading has the verb as “so that he brings out,” with people as its subject.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p406/r3.anchor: وقرىء: ليخرج مضارع خرج بالياء بنقطتين من تحتها، والناس رفع به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p406/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p406/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p406/r4.claim: The phrase “to the light” is clarified by “to a path”; the attributes of might and praise correspond respectively to revelation of the Book and guidance from darkness to faith, and their order follows those two matters.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p406/r4.anchor: ولما كان قوله: إلى النور، فيه إبهام ما أوضحه بقوله: إلى صراط

NAHHAS:v2p363/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p363/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p363/r1.claim: The opening identifies this as a book sent down to the Prophet; the phrase is nominative as an adjective of “Book.”
NAHHAS:v2p363/r1.anchor: أي هذا كتاب أنزلناه إليك في موضع رفع على النعت لكتاب

NAHHAS:v2p363/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p363/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p363/r2.claim: The lām in “to bring people out” marks purpose, with the implied wording “so that people may come out.”
NAHHAS:v2p363/r2.anchor: لتخرج الناس ) لام كي والتقدير ليخرج الناس

NAHHAS:v2p363/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p363/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p363/r3.claim: Idhn is used figuratively to mean command.

RAZI-FULL:v19p66/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p66/r4.speaker: أبو مسلم الأصفهاني
RAZI-FULL:v19p66/r4.claim: Abu Muslim sees the parallel between Muhammad’s and Moses’ missions as showing that all prophets share one purpose: bringing people from the darkness of error to the light of guidance.
RAZI-FULL:v19p66/r4.anchor: والمقصود : بيان أن المقصود من البعثة واحد في حق جميع الأنبياء عليهم السلام

TABATABAI:14:1-5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:1-5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:1-5/r1.claim: God has purposes in creation and command, but these purposes return to His creatures rather than completing or benefiting Him.
TABATABAI:14:1-5/r1.anchor: فلله سبحانه في خلقه وأمره أغراض، وإن كان لا يستكمل بأغراض أفعاله كما نستكمل نحن

TABATABAI:14:1-5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:1-5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:1-5/r2.claim: God is not governed by intellect or compelled by benefit and harm; He guides reason and shows benefits and harms what they entail.
TABATABAI:14:1-5/r2.anchor: فلا يكون تعالى محكوما بعقل بل هو الذي يهدي العقل إلى ما يعقله

TABATABAI:14:1-5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:1-5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:1-5/r3.claim: Welfare is inferred from God's action: His act depends on being beneficial, but benefit does not rule His essence or force Him to act.
TABATABAI:14:1-5/r3.anchor: فالغرض والمصلحة منتزعة من مقام فعله بمعنى أن فعله يتوقف على المصلحة لكنها لا تحكم في ذاته تعالى

TABATABAI:14:1-5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:1-5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:1-5/r4.claim: Unlike humans, God does not achieve self-completion through the ends of His actions, and neither welfare nor harm compels Him.
TABATABAI:14:1-5/r4.anchor: غرضه في فعله يفارق أغراضنا في أفعالنا من وجهين أحدهما أنه تعالى لا يستكمل بأغراض أفعاله

TABATABAI:14:1-5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:1-5/r5.speaker: الأشاعرة والمعتزلة
TABATABAI:14:1-5/r5.claim: The familiar dispute asks whether real welfare governs divine action and inclines God to act, or whether His acts have no end and are arbitrary; this passage does not assign the two formulations to particular sides.
TABATABAI:14:1-5/r5.anchor: النزاع المعروف بين الأشاعرة والمعتزلة في أن أفعال الله معللة بالأغراض أم لا

TABATABAI:14:1-5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:1-5/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:1-5/r6.claim: After full examination, the author rejects both poles of that debate and says the truth lies between them, with a fuller rational and transmitted discussion promised later.
TABATABAI:14:1-5/r6.anchor: والحق خلاف القولين جميعا، وهو أمر بين الأمرين

TABATABAI:14:1-5#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:1-5#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:1-5#2/r1.claim: The surah's argument turns on God's oneness in lordship, might, and praiseworthiness in action, so people should fear Him, thank Him, trust His promise, and remember His signs.
TABATABAI:14:1-5#2/r1.anchor: فجل الكلام في هذه السورة فيما يقتضيه الصفات الثلاث توحده تعالى بالربوبية وعزته وكونه حميدا في أفعاله

SAMIN-DURR:14:1/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:1/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:1/r1.claim: كتاب can predicate ألر as subject, be predicate of omitted هذا, or be a subject whose following clause is predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:14:1/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { كتاب أنزلناه إليك }: يجوز أن يرتفع خبرا ل " ألر " إن قلنا إنها مبتدأ

SAMIN-DURR:14:1/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:1/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:1/r2.claim: On the subject parse, the indefinite may begin the sentence because it is implicitly qualified: a great book distinguished among the heavenly books.
SAMIN-DURR:14:1/r2.anchor: وجاز الابتداء بالنكرة لأنها موصوفة تقديرا. تقديره: كتاب أي كتاب، يعني عظيما من بين الكتب السماوية.

SAMIN-DURR:14:1/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:1/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:1/r3.claim: The purpose clause attaches to أنزلنا. A reading ليخرج الناس has third-person yāʾ and nominative الناس as its subject.
SAMIN-DURR:14:1/r3.anchor: قوله: " لتخرج " متعلق ب " أنزلنا " وقرئ " ليخرج الناس " بفتح الياء وضم الراء

SAMIN-DURR:14:1/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:1/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:1/r4.claim: بإذن may modify bringing people out, meaning by facilitation, or be circumstantial to the subject of تخرج as authorized.
SAMIN-DURR:14:1/r4.anchor: قوله: " بإذن " يجوز أن يتعلق بالإخراج، أي: بتسهيله وتيسيره

SAMIN-DURR:14:1/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:1/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:1/r5.claim: إلى صراط may replace إلى النور with the preposition repeated, or attach to an omitted phrase answering an implied question: to what light? To a path.
SAMIN-DURR:14:1/r5.anchor: قوله: { إلى صراط } فيه وجهان، أحدهما: أنه بدل من قوله { إلى النور } بإعادة العامل

ZAJJAJ:v3p153/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p153/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p153/r1.claim: The sura is Meccan except for two verses revealed in Medina, beginning with ألم تر إلى الذين بدلوا نعمت الله and ending with وبئس القرار.
ZAJJAJ:v3p153/r1.anchor: مكية إلا اثنتين منها نزلت بالمدينة

ZAJJAJ:v3p153/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p153/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p153/r2.claim: كتاب is nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject: the sense is, This is a Book We sent down to you.
ZAJJAJ:v3p153/r2.anchor: مرفوع على خبر الابتداء، المعنى هذا كتاب أنزلناه إليك.

ZAJJAJ:v3p153/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p153/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ZAJJAJ:v3p153/r3.claim: Some parse كتاب as governed by الر; Zajjaj rejects this because the initials are only a part of the Book, whose whole is the verses and recitation.
ZAJJAJ:v3p153/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم كتاب مرتفع بقوله (الر) و (الر) ليست هي الكتاب إنما هي شيء من الكتاب.

ZAJJAJ:v3p153/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p153/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p153/r4.claim: Disbelief is likened to darkness because it is obscure, while manifest, luminous faith is likened to light.
ZAJJAJ:v3p153/r4.anchor: ما كانوا فيه من الكفر، لأن الكفر غير بين فمثل بالظلمات.

ZAJJAJ:v3p153/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p153/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p153/r5.claim: The preposition may attach to تُخرج, meaning by God's permission to teach them; alternatively, no one is guided except by God's permission and will.
ZAJJAJ:v3p153/r5.anchor: أي بما أذن الله لك من تعليمهم، ويجوز أن يكون بإذن ربهم

ZAJJAJ:v3p153/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p153/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p153/r6.claim: الحميد is genitive as an adjective of العزيز; it may instead be nominative as a new subject with الله as predicate, with other subject-predicate inflections also possible.
ZAJJAJ:v3p153/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يرفع الله ويخفض (الحميد) على ما وصفنا.

ASAD-NOTES:14:1#n1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:1#n1/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:1#n1/r1.claim: Asad directs readers to Appendix II and his note on surah 11:1 for discussion of the opening letters.
ASAD-NOTES:14:1#n1/r1.anchor: See Appendix II; also surah 11, note 1.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p156/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p156/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p156/r1.claim: The opening letters indicate that the inimitable Quran is made from the familiar letters Arabs use, yet they cannot produce its like; openings followed by declarations of the Book's revelation support this reading.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p156/r1.anchor: القائلون بأنها إشارة إلى أن القرآن المعجز جاء من مألوف حروفهم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p156/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p156/r2.speaker: ابن كثير
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p156/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir supports the inimitability reading: people cannot match the Quran although it is composed of the same disjoint letters they use; al-Razi, al-Qurtubi, al-Zamakhshari, Ibn Taymiyya, and al-Mizzi are also cited in support or transmission of it.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p156/r2.anchor: وينتصر الحافظ ابن كثير لهذا المذهب في مجئ هذه الحروف

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p156/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p156/r3.speaker: محمد رشيد رضا
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p156/r3.claim: Rashid Rida reproduces nearly the same argument while commenting on Muhammad Abduh's alternative that these are names for the suras beginning with them.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p156/r3.anchor: قد نقله السيد محمد رشيد رضا، معقباً به على قول الشيخ محمد عبده

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p175/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p175/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p175/r1.claim: After five suras without disjoint-letter openings, the renewed objections of the polytheists are answered in Ibrahim and al-Sajdah, which reopen with letters beside statements affirming revelation and rebutting their arguments.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p175/r1.anchor: بعد الحواميم، نزلت خمس سور بغير فواتح من الحروف المقطعة، وكان المتوقع أن ينتهي جدل المشركين في المعجزة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Where 13:41 warned Quraysh and promised Muslim success indirectly, Surah Ibrāhīm states both warning and glad tidings explicitly.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the Quryash were threatened by the words “Do they not see that We are closing in upon this territory by reducing it from its borders?”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Quraysh’s evil message is rootless like a tree grown from filth and will soon be removed by those God has sent to uproot it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: It is like an evil tree that has grown from garbage and dirt. It does not have any roots

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Islam’s message is a deeply rooted evergreen tree; God will strengthen believers in this life and the Hereafter if they persevere in delivering truth and trust Him through trials.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: example of Islam’s message is that of an evergreen tree which is very deeply rooted and whose branches are spread in the sky.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Moses’ and other prophets’ stories reinforce the theme; Abraham’s migration, prayer for Arabia, and hopes for his descendants mirror Quraysh’s history and what was expected of them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: migration from his homeland to the desolate desert of Arabia is referred to and the supplication he offered for this land is alluded to.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Qur’an is revealed to the Prophet so that, by God’s leave, he may lead people from evil beliefs and deeds into true faith and righteous action.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the Qur’ ān has been revealed so the he can take people out from the darkness of their evil beliefs and misdeeds to the light

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Islahi says his treatment of the isolated letters appears at the beginning of his discussion of al-Baqarah.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: I have comprehensively dealt with the isolated letters

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The expansive darkness is the darkness of faith and deeds; the light is faith and righteous deeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Expansive darkness here refers to the darkness of faith and deeds and light here refers to the light of faith and righteous deeds.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Many paths lead astray while guidance has one path, which explains the plural for darkness and singular for light.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: For this reason, the word used for darkness occurs in the plural and that for light in the singular.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Only those whom God gives an urge for guidance will be brought from darkness to light; He guides the deserving and leaves those who deserve it to stray.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: only they will be led to light from darkness who are provided its urge from God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The prophet's responsibility is to communicate the message; bringing people to the path of truth is not his duty.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the responsibility of the prophet is to only communicate the message

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The light is the path leading to God; because He is mighty He alone is to be feared, and because He is praiseworthy He alone deserves praise and hope.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The last part of the verse “to the path of the God Who is powerful; has all praiseworthy attributes” explains the word “light.”

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p25/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p25/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p25/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisai read al-ḥamīd and Allah in the genitive, with Allah as an appositive.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p25/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p25/r2.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p25/r2.claim: Nafi and Ibn Amir read the phrase with nominative case; Hafs agrees with Abu Amr, and the source notes no other transmission of this from Nafi.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p25/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر: (الحميد* الله) رفعا

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p25/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p25/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p25/r3.claim: In the genitive reading, Allah is appositional rather than adjectival: although the name began as a verbal noun, verbal nouns can serve as adjectives.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p25/r3.anchor: من جر جعله بدلا من الحميد ، ولم يكن صفة

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p202#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p202#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p202#2/r1.claim: Rafʿ on Allāh treats al-ḥamīd as a complete verse-end and begins a new sentence with Allāh as subject.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p202#2/r1.anchor: فالحجة لمن رفع أنه جعل الكلام تاما عند قوله الحميد ثم ابتدأ قوله الله الذي فرفعه بالابتداء وإنما حسن ذلك لأن الذي قبله رأس آية

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p202#2/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p202#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p202#2/r2.claim: Kasra on Allāh makes it an appositive or adjective modifying al-ḥamīd.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p202#2/r2.anchor: والحجة لمن خفض أنه جعله بدلا من قوله الحميد أو نعتا له

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p202#2/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p202#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p202#2/r3.claim: Basran grammarians distinguish adjective from apposition: a following epithet identifies someone by name, while a preceding epithet followed by the name is apposition.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p202#2/r3.anchor: فما كان حلية للإنسان جاءت بعد اسمه ليفرق بذلك بينه وبين غيره ممن له هذا الاسم فهو النعت

IBNMUJAHID:v1p362/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p362/r1.speaker: ابن كثير، أبو عمرو، عاصم، حمزة، الكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p362/r1.claim: These readers construe الله as a بدل after الحميد; Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read الله nominative.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p362/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم وحمزة والكسائى ﴿ الحميد الله ﴾ على البدل

IBNMUJAHID:v1p362/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p362/r2.speaker: نافع عن الأصمعي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p362/r2.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī reports genitive الله from Nāfiʿ, like Abū ʿAmr; Ibn Mujāhid says no one else transmits this from Nāfiʿ.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p362/r2.anchor: وحدثنى عبيد الله بن على عن نصر بن على عن الأصمعى عن نافع ﴿ الله ﴾ خفضا مثل أبى عمرو ولم يرو عن نافع ذلك غيره

QIRAAT-ER:14:1:1#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:14:1:1#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:14:1:1#1/r1.claim: The waqf reading pronounces each of the letters separately, with sukūn or pause markers, emphasizing each as a distinct unit.
QIRAAT-ER:14:1:1#1/r1.anchor: Waqf reading: each letter separated with sukūn/pause markers — emphasizes individual pronunciation

QIRAAT-ER:14:1:16#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:14:1:16#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:14:1:16#1/r1.claim: The sīn-for-ṣād pronunciation is linked to a possible Syriac etymology from strata, without semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:14:1:16#1/r1.anchor: Sīn replaces ṣād — pronunciation variant reflecting the possible etymology from strata via Syriac

QIRAAT-ER:14:1:16#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:14:1:16#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:14:1:16#2/r1.claim: Ishmām gives ṣād a slight zāy quality, producing a phonetic midpoint between ṣād and sīn; it is a canonical variant.
QIRAAT-ER:14:1:16#2/r1.anchor: Ishmām: the ṣād is pronounced with a slight zāy quality

QIRAAT-ER:14:1:18#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:14:1:18#1/r1.speaker: some readers
QIRAAT-ER:14:1:18#1/r1.claim: Some readers connect al-ḥamīdi to Allāhi in the genitive as an apposition or attribute, identifying the Praiseworthy as God across the verse boundary.
QIRAAT-ER:14:1:18#1/r1.anchor: Continuation into 14:2: some readers connect al-ḥamīdi directly to Allāhi (genitive)

QIRAAT-ER:14:1:18#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:14:1:18#2/r1.speaker: some readers
QIRAAT-ER:14:1:18#2/r1.claim: Other readers take Allāhu in the nominative as the subject of a new sentence beginning the next verse, syntactically separating it from al-ḥamīdi.
QIRAAT-ER:14:1:18#2/r1.anchor: Continuation into 14:2: Allāhu in nominative — beginning a new sentence

QIRAAT-ER:14:1:18#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:14:1:18#3/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:14:1:18#3/r1.claim: The ten-reader tradition attests both genitive and nominative linkage after al-ḥamīdi, making the verse boundary a site of variant parsing.
QIRAAT-ER:14:1:18#3/r1.anchor: 10-reader tradition attests both genitive and nominative linkage for Allāh after al-ḥamīdi

ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r1.claim: Kitāb may be a predicate for alif-lām-rā, a predicate of an omitted subject, an object of an omitted verb, a title in an enumeration, a second predicate, or a subject licensed by an understood adjective such as “great.”
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r1.anchor: جوز فيه أن يكون خبرا لألر على تقدير كونه مبتدأ أو لمبتدأ مضمر

ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r2.claim: The clause anzalnāhu ilayka can be an adjective or predicate; together with its related elements it is also said to explain the preceding construction.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r2.anchor: إما في موضع الصفة أو الخبر وهو مع مبتدآته قيل في موضع التفسير

ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r3.claim: The majestic plural in “We sent it down” and direct address to the Prophet, followed by assigning him the task of bringing people out, heighten the verse’s honorific force.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r3.anchor: وفي إسناد الإنزال إلى ضمير العظمة ومخاطبته عليه الصلاة والسلام مع إسناد الإخراج إليه صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r4.claim: The purpose lām is attached to anzalnāhu, and al-nās means all people: the book is sent to bring them out through clear proofs of divine origin and true belief.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r4.anchor: واللام متعلقة ( بأنزلناه ) والمراد من الناس جميعهم أي أنزلناه إليك

ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r5.claim: The plural darknesses represent false beliefs and worship of multiple alleged deities, while the singular light is truth founded on God’s oneness.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r5.anchor: الكاشفة عن العقائد الحقة من عقائد الكفر والضلال وعبادة الله عز وجل من الآلهة المختلفة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r6.claim: A reading with yāʾ instead of tāʾ has “so that the people may be brought out,” with al-nās in the nominative as the verb’s subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r6.anchor: وقريء ( ليخرج الناس ) بالياء التحتانية في ( يخرج ) ورفع ( الناس ) به

ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r7.claim: Permission means God’s enabling and granting success; it is metaphorically likened to permission that clears a barrier for someone seeking arrival.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r7.anchor: أي بتيسيره وتوفيقه تعالى وهو مستعار من الإذن الذي يوجب تسهيل الحجاب

ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r8.speaker: محيي السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r8.claim: Muḥyī al-Sunna interprets God’s permission as His command; other reported glosses are His knowledge or will, which al-Ālūsī says are close in meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r8.anchor: وقال محي السنة : إذنه تعالى أمره وقيل : علمه سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r9.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r9.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects interpreting permission as command or knowledge, though al-Ālūsī says his reasoning is not free of difficulty.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r9.anchor: ومنع الإمام أن يراد بذلك الأمر أو العلم وعلله بما لايخلو عن نظر

ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r10.claim: On the enabling reading, the verse contains three metaphors: permission and the paired images of darkness and light.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r10.anchor: وفي الكلام على ماذكر أولا ثلاث استعارات احداها ماسمعت في الأذن

ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r11.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r11.claim: Al-Ṭībī reads the whole expression as a composite metaphor: a lost person in a dark wilderness is rescued by a royal writ securing help, as the messenger and book guide the disbeliever toward faith by divine favor.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r11.anchor: جوز العلامة الطيبي أن تكون كلها استعارة مركبة تمثيلية بتصوير الهدى بالنور والضلال بالظلمة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r12.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r12.claim: The wording uses “their Lord” where “Our Lord” might be expected to signal divine nurturing, kindness, and grace; guidance is a pure favor.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r12.anchor: وقيل : ( ربهم ) للاشعار بالتربية واللطف والفضل

ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r13.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r13.claim: The composite image emphasizes that book, messenger, and invitation do not suffice without God’s permission, as 28:56 states.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r13.anchor: وفيه أن الكتاب والرسول والدعوة لاتجدي دون اذن الله تعالى كما قال سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r14.claim: Al-Ālūsī finds al-Ṭībī’s composite metaphor eloquent but somewhat remote, and relates enabling to turning toward truth, as in 13:27.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r14.anchor: وما ذكره من الاستعارة التمثيلية مع بلاغته وحسنه لايخلو عن بعد وكأنه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r15.claim: “Their Lord” signals nurture, which brings the guided toward their perfection; permission’s broad meaning includes everyone even though its effect does not manifest in those with bad choices and dispositions.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r15.anchor: استعير لذلك الإذن الذي هو ما علمت وأضيف إلى ضمير الناس اسم الرب المفصح عن التربية

ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r16.speaker: الطبرسي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r16.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī takes the lām as result rather than purpose, lest all people become believers; al-Ālūsī rejects this because the purpose is universal guidance and some refuse it through their own choices.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r16.anchor: ومن هنا فساد قول الطبرسي : إن اللام لام الغرض لا لام العاقبة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r17.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r17.claim: Al-Rāzī says the Muʿtazila cite the purpose clause for the view that God’s acts are explained by beneficial purposes; he gives the opposing argument for impossibility and says such verses then require reinterpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r17.anchor: وذكر الإمام أن المعتزلة استدلوا بهذه الآية على أن أفعال الله تعالى تعلل برعاية المصالح ثم ساق دليل أصحابه على امتناع ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r18.speaker: ابن القيم وغيره
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r18.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim and others call purposive explanation the position of the Salaf and cite more than ten thousand apparent scriptural examples; al-Ālūsī finds no compelling proof of impossibility and says universal reinterpretation is unfair.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r18.anchor: ونقل عن ابن القيم وغيره القول بالتعليل وأنه مذهب السلف وأن في الكتاب والسنة مايزيد على عشرة آلاف موضع ظاهره في ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r19.claim: The prepositional phrase most naturally modifies takhrija; alternatively it is a circumstantial phrase describing the people brought out or the agent who brings them out.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r19.anchor: والباء متعلقة بتخرج على ماهو الظاهر وجوز أن يكون متعلقا بمضمر وقع حالا من مفعوله

ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r20.claim: Those who require instruction from a messenger for knowledge of God cite the Prophet’s role in bringing people from darkness to guidance; the response is that he alerts them, while knowledge comes from proof.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r20.anchor: واستدل بالآية القائلون بأن معرفة الله تعالى لاتحصل الا من طريق التعليم من الرسول

ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r21.claim: Both Muʿtazilites and Sunnis cite the verse for their positions on human acts; al-Ālūsī refers readers to al-Rāzī for details.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p180/r21.anchor: واستدل بها أيضا كل من المعتزلة وأهل السنة على مذهبه في أفعال العباد

ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r1.claim: The phrase ilā ṣirāṭ may be a prepositional substitute for ilā al-nūr, or ṣirāṭ may substitute for al-nūr with its governing preposition repeated, as in 7:75.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r1.anchor: الجار والمجرور بدل من الجار والمجرور فيما تقدم أعني قوله تعالى : ( إلى النور )

ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r2.claim: The substitution does not spoil the earlier metaphor: guidance is first light for its clarity, then a safe, well-guided road rather than a treacherous path through desire.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r2.anchor: جعل نورا أولا لظهوره في نفسه واستضاءة الضلال في مهواة الهوى به ثم جعل ثانيا جادة مسلوكة مأمونة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r3.speaker: الإرشاد
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r3.claim: Al-Irshād notes that apposition or explanation undermines metaphor only in literal usage, not figurative usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r3.anchor: وفي الإرشاد أن إخلال البيان والبدل بالاستعارة إنما هو في الحقيقة لا في المجاز

ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r4.claim: Alternatively, the phrase modifies an omitted clause answering “to what light?”: “to a path.”
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r4.anchor: جواب سائل يسأل إلى أي نور فقيل : ( إلى صراط )

ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r5.claim: The path is attributed to God because He is its destination or the one who makes it clear.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r5.anchor: وإضافة الصراط إليه تعالى لأنه مقصده أو المبين له

ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r6.claim: Mentioning these two attributes encourages following the path: it is hard to tread, and its walker is praised.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r6.anchor: إذ في ذلك إشارة إلى أنه يعز سلوكه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r7.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān links the names to the preceding acts: al-ʿAzīz signals the power behind sending the inimitable book, and al-Ḥamīd the blessing of guiding people from darkness to light.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r7.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : النكتة في ذلك أنه لما ذكر قبل إنزاله تعالى لهذا الكتاب وإخراج الناس

ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r8.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r8.claim: Al-Rāzī says al-ʿAzīz means powerful and al-Ḥamīd knowledgeable and self-sufficient; power is named first because knowledge of power precedes knowledge of God’s knowledge and independence.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r8.anchor: وقال الإمام : إنما قدم ذكر ( العزيز ) على ذكر ( الحميد ) لأن الصحيح أن أول العلم بالله تعالى العلم بكونه تعالى قادرا

ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r9.claim: Al-Ālūsī says al-Ḥamīd is not otherwise glossed as knowledgeable and self-sufficient; it means the praised one, praised by Himself eternally and by His servants forever.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r9.anchor: وغيرهما أن ( الحميد ) هو المحمود المثنى عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r10.claim: Al-ʿAzīz is also explained as the One without an equal or likeness.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p181/r10.anchor: فهو قول لبعضهم وقيل : هو الذي لامثل له

ALUSI-FULL:v13p182/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p182/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p182/r1.claim: One may explain the order as giving priority to negative attributes, in keeping with purification before adornment and the order in 42:11.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p182/r1.anchor: وربما يقال على هذا : إن التقديم للاعتناء بالصفات السلبية كما يؤذن به قولهم : التخلية أولى من التحلية

ALUSI-FULL:v13p182/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p182/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p182/r2.claim: Al-Ālūsī concludes that al-Rāzī’s preceding explanation of the order remains open to question.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p182/r2.anchor: ولعل كلامه قدس سره بعد لايخلو عن نظر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p329#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p329#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p329#2/r1.claim: The book sent to Muḥammad is the Qurʾān.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p329#2/r1.anchor: {الر كتاب} أي: هذا كتاب {أنزلناه إليك} يا محمد يعني: القرآن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p329#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p329#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p329#2/r2.claim: The Qurʾān was sent so the Prophet could call people from the darkness of error to the light of faith.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p329#2/r2.anchor: {لتخرج الناس من الظلمات إلى النور} أي: لتدعوهم من ظلمات الضلالة إلى نور الإيمان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p329#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p329#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p329#2/r3.claim: One explanation takes bi-idhn rabbihim to mean by their Lord's command.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p329#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p329#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p329#2/r4.claim: Another explanation takes it to mean by their Lord's knowledge.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p329#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p329#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p329#2/r5.claim: The path is God's religion; al-ʿAzīz means the all-dominant and al-Ḥamīd the one deserving praise.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p329#2/r5.anchor: {إلى صراط العزيز الحميد} أي: إلى دينه، و"العزيز"، هو الغالب، و"الحميد": هو المستحق للحمد

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r2.claim: The opening means: this is a book.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r3.claim: Through calling people to what the book contains, the Prophet brings them out of darkness into light.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r3.anchor: { أنزلنه إليك لتخرج الناس } بدعائك إياهم إلى ما تضمنه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r4.claim: The darknesses are the various kinds of misguidance.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r6.claim: Permission means God’s enabling and facilitation, metaphorically borrowed from permission as the easing of a barrier.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r6.anchor: { بإذن ربهم } بتوفيقه وتسهيله مستعار من الاذن الذي هو تسهيل الحجاب

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r7.claim: The phrase may attach to li-tukhrij or function circumstantially with its subject or object.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r7.anchor: وهو صلة { لتخرج } أو حال من فاعله أو مفعوله.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r8.claim: The path phrase may be an appositive to the light with the preposition repeated, or a fresh answer to an implied question.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r8.anchor: { إلى صراط العزيز الحميد } بدل من قوله: { إلى النور } بتكرير العامل أو استئناف على أنه جواب لمن يسأل عنه

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r9.claim: The path is attributed to God because He is its destination or makes it manifest.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r9.anchor: وإضافة الصراط إلى الله تعالى إما لأنه مقصده أو المظهر له

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r10.claim: These attributes signal that the path’s traveler will not be humiliated or disappointed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:1/r10.anchor: وتخصيص الوصفين للتنبيه على أنه لا يذل سالكه ولا يخيب سابله

BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r1.claim: Sūrat Ibrāhīm is Meccan and has fifty-two verses.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r1.anchor: سورة إبراهيم مكية - آياتها اثنان وخمسون

BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r2.claim: The basmala names God as uniquely perfect and without equal, merciful to all creation through a supremely clear Book, and especially gracious to servants He chooses.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r2.anchor: تفرد بالكمال , وعز عن أن يكون له كفو أو مثال

BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r3.claim: The sūra's purpose is affirming God's oneness and showing the Book as a complete guide to the path leading to Him; its secrets move creation from one stage to another, signaled by the letter rāʾ.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r3.anchor: مقصود السورة التوحيد , وبيان أن هذا الكتاب

BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r4.claim: Abraham's story is the sūra's clearest evidence: it affirms oneness and connects the Book to Abraham's prayer for a messenger among his descendants.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r4.anchor: وأدل ما فيها على هذا المرام قصة إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام

BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r5.claim: The preceding sūra ended by saying that no testimony matches the testimony of one who has knowledge of the Book; the Qur'an itself testifies through its inimitable eloquence and knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r5.anchor: ختم الرعد بأنه لا شهادة تكافىء شهادة من عنده علم الكتاب إشارة إلى أن الكتاب هو الشاهد بإعجازه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r6.claim: Earlier sūras called the Book wise, firmly composed, detailed, clear, and true; here its indefinite form magnifies it beyond ordinary description.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r6.anchor: تكرر وصفه في سورة يونس وهود ويوسف والرعد بأنه حكيم محكم مفصل مبين

BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r7.claim: The indefinite Book is an expression of glorification: its greatness exceeds what human minds can describe.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r7.anchor: منكرا تنكير التعظيم فقال : { كتاب } أي عظيم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r8.claim: God revealed it to the Messenger in his people's language so he could explain it to them.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r8.anchor: بما لنا من العظمة { إليك } بلسان قومك لتبين لهم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r9.claim: The Book and the Prophet's call bring all people, despite their confusion, out of the many forms of misguidance caused by ignorance into God's single path.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r9.anchor: التي هي أنواع كثيرة من الضلالات التي أدت إليها الجهالات

BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p165#2/r10.claim: Alternatively, the phrase concerns clarifying the message fully to the Arabs in their own language through decisive arguments, making the way to faith unmistakable.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p166/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p166/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p166/r1.claim: Faith is likened to light because it protects reason from error on the way to God, as physical light protects sight from losing the road; those guided can then guide others.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p166/r1.anchor: وشبه الإيمان وما أرشد إليه بالنور

BIQAI-FULL:v4p166/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p166/r2.speaker: الرماني
BIQAI-FULL:v4p166/r2.claim: Al-Rummānī says permission originally means release to act through speech heard by the ear.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p166/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p166/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p166/r3.claim: The light is clarified as the path of the Mighty, who is free from deficiency and cannot be challenged or have its travelers harmed without His leave.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p166/r3.anchor: فعز عن أن يدخل أحد صراطه الذي هو ربه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p166/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p166/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p166/r4.claim: The Praiseworthy possesses every perfection and deserves praise both for Himself and for the blessings by which He nurtures His servants.

BURSEVI:v4p260/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p260/r1.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v4p260/r1.claim: Al-Kāshifī reports that some take these disconnected letters as names of the Qur'an, and gloss alif-lām-rā as Qur'an or Book.
BURSEVI:v4p260/r1.anchor: وفي تفسير الكاشفي : (جمعي بر آنندكه اين حروف

BURSEVI:v4p260/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p260/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p260/r2.claim: The Book was sent to Muhammad through Gabriel as a miraculous proof of his prophethood, in keeping with the later reference to Moses being sent with signs.
BURSEVI:v4p260/r2.anchor: أنزلناه إليك يا محمد بواسطة جبرائيل حال كونه حجة على رسالتك بإعجازه يناسب قوله تعالى فيما بعد ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا

BURSEVI:v4p260/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p260/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p260/r3.claim: The Prophet's call and guidance bring all people from misguidance, disbelief, hypocrisy, doubt, and innovation to guidance, faith, sincerity, certainty, and Sunna through the Book's true beliefs and beneficial rulings.
BURSEVI:v4p260/r3.anchor: لتخرج الناس كافة بدعائك وإرشادك إياهم إلى ما تضمنه الكتاب من العقائد الحقة والأحكام النافعة

BURSEVI:v4p260/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p260/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p260/r4.claim: Inwardly, emergence means moving from multiplicity to unity, from veils of acts and attributes to the unity of essence, and from createdness to the manifestation of divine lordship.
BURSEVI:v4p260/r4.anchor: ومن ظلمة الكثرة إلى نور الوحدة ومن ظلمة حجب الأفعال وأستار الصفات إلى نور وحدة الذات ومن ظلمة الخلقية إلى نور تجلى صفة الربوبية

BURSEVI:v4p260/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p260/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p260/r5.claim: The spirit-world is made of light and its quintessence is human spirit; this material world is bodies and its quintessence is human body. Bodily qualities veil the spirit, and both worlds veil divinity.
BURSEVI:v4p260/r5.anchor: خلق عالم الآخرة وهو عالم الأرواح من النور وجعل زبدته روح الإنسان

BURSEVI:v4p260/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p260/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p260/r6.claim: A tradition speaks of seventy thousand veils of light and darkness; only humans have the capacity to leave them, and believers receive this honor through God's guardianship and the Prophet and Qur'an as means.
BURSEVI:v4p260/r6.anchor: إنسبعين حجابا من نور وظلمة لو كشفت لأحرقت سبحات وجه

BURSEVI:v4p260/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p260/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p260/r7.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya says their Lord's permission means God's power, since the Prophet cannot guide independently; the wording their Lord marks the act as God's nurturing, not the Prophet's.
BURSEVI:v4p260/r7.anchor: وما قال بإذن ربك ليعلم إن هذه التربية من الله

BURSEVI:v4p260#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p260#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p260#3/r1.claim: To the path of the Mighty and Praiseworthy is an appositive to to the light, with the preposition repeated; the path is Islam, leading to Paradise, nearness, and union.
BURSEVI:v4p260#3/r1.anchor: بدل من قوله إلى النور بتكرير العامل وإضافة الصراط إلى العزيز

BURSEVI:v4p260#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p260#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p260#3/r2.claim: Al-ʿAzīz is the overpowering one who avenges the enemies of His religion; al-Ḥamīd is the praised one who thereby merits His servants' praise.

BURSEVI:v4p260#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p260#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p260#3/r3.claim: Inwardly, crossing bodily darkness and spiritual lights is the way to God: reaching Him requires leaving veils, while His beauty and majesty merit veiling by might and grandeur.
BURSEVI:v4p260#3/r3.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن العبور على الظلمات الجسمانية والأنوار الروحانية هو الطريق إلى الله تعالى

DURR-FULL:v5p3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Zubayr report that Sura Ibrahim was revealed in Mecca.
DURR-FULL:v5p3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس - رضي الله عنهما - قال نزلت سورة إبراهيم عليه السلام بمكة

DURR-FULL:v5p3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the sura is Meccan except the two verses about those exchanging God’s favor for disbelief, revealed in Medina concerning Badr’s slain polytheists.
DURR-FULL:v5p3/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس - رضي الله عنهما - قال: سورة إبراهيم عليه السلام نزلت بمكة سوى آيتين نزلتا بالمدينة وهما: {ألم تر إلى الذين بدلوا نعمة الله كفرا}

DURR-FULL:v5p3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p3/r3.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p3/r3.claim: The sura is classified as Meccan and counted as fifty-two verses.
DURR-FULL:v5p3/r3.anchor: سورة إبراهيم مكية وآياتها ثنتان وخمسون

DURR-FULL:v5p3/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p3/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p3/r4.claim: Qatada explains bringing people from darkness to light as leading them from error to guidance.
DURR-FULL:v5p3/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {لتخرج الناس من الظلمات إلى النور} قال: من الضلالة إلى الهدى

DURR-FULL:v5p3/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p3/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Muhammad was favored over angels by a promise of forgiveness, unlike the threat to any angel claiming divinity (21:29; 48:2).
DURR-FULL:v5p3/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس - رضي الله عنهما - قال: إن الله فضل محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم على أهل السماء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r1.claim: The purpose of revelation is to guide people: God did not leave them astray. The guided follow His direction; those who stray choose desire over guidance’s evidence, and God’s commands serve wisdom and interests of varying importance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r1.anchor: وتعليل الإنزال بالإخراج من الظلمات دل على أن الهداية هي مراد الله تعالى من الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r2.claim: ‘Bringing out’ is a metaphor for moving people from one state to another, with transition likened to exit and the act of moving likened to bringing out.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r2.anchor: شبه الانتقال بالخروج فشبه النقل بالإخراج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r3.claim: Darkness and light metaphorically represent disbelief and faith: disbelief confuses, while faith guides to truth. The hearer may picture a bewildered person emerging from darkness into a bright place.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r3.anchor: استعارة للكفر والإيمان ، لأن الكفر يجعل صاحبه في حيرة فهو كالظلمة في ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r4.claim: The plural ‘darknesses’ and singular ‘light’ were explained at the beginning of al-Anʿam.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r5.claim: The bāʾ is causal. Permission is a command to act that depends on the commander’s consent; here it is God’s authorization of the Messenger’s mission, as in the statement that every messenger is sent to be obeyed by God’s permission.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r5.anchor: للسببية ، والإذن : الأمر بفعل يتوقف على رضى الآمر به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r6.claim: Because the sending is for people’s benefit, permission is attributed to their Lord, who manages their interests.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r6.anchor: ولما كان الإرسال لمصلحتهم أضيف الإذن إلى وصف الرب المضاف إلى ضمير الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r7.claim: ‘To the path’ is apposition to ‘the light’; the repeated preposition elaborates the appositive and gives it emphasis, as in the cited wording from al-Aʿraf.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r7.anchor: إلى صراط العزيز الحميد ( سورة إبراهيم : 1 ) بدل من النور } بإعادة الجار للمبدل منه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r8.claim: The metaphor of the path for true religion suits the imagery of bringing people from darkness into light and its implied comparison.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r8.anchor: ومناسبة الصراط المستعار للدين الحق ، لاستعارة الإخراج والظلمات والنور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r9.claim: These attributes best suit the context: the unconquerable God’s revealed Book proves His purpose right, overcomes opponents, and establishes the proof against them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p180/r9.anchor: لأن العزيز الذي لا يغلب . وإنزال الكتاب برهان على أحقية ما أراده الله من الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p181#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p181#2/r1.speaker: نافع، وابن عامر، وأبو جعفر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p181#2/r1.claim: These readers put the name Allah in the nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject: ‘He—the Mighty, Praiseworthy—is God, to whom belongs all in the heavens and earth.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p181#2/r1.anchor: قرأ نافع ، وابن عامر ، وأبو جعفر برفع اسم الجلالة على أنه خبر عن مبتدإ محذوف .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p181#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p181#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p181#2/r2.claim: The omitted subject follows a familiar Arabic usage: after describing someone, speakers move to a more consequential predicate, reinforcing the purpose; al-Sakkākī calls this omission to follow usage. The cited couplets by Ibrāhīm al-Ṣūlī exemplify the omitted ‘he’ before فتى.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p181#2/r2.anchor: وهذا الحذف جار على حذف المسند إليه المسمى عند علماء المعاني تبعا للسكاكي بالحذف لمتابعة الاستعمال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p181#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p181#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p181#2/r5.claim: Both readings reach the same point: Allah is more worthy of mention after the prior attributes, though the nominative is more emphatic. The relative clause magnifies Him rather than identifying Him, since the audience already knows Him as owner of all beings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p181#2/r5.anchor: ومآل القراءتين واحد وكلتا الطريقتين تفيد أن المنتقل إليه أجدر بالذكر عقب ما تقدمه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p181#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p181#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p181#2/r6.claim: The relative clause indirectly rebukes idolaters: the path of anything besides God cannot reach its destination because its objects are deficient, and their idols do not own the heavens and earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p181#2/r6.anchor: وفيه تعريض بأن صراط غير الله من طرق آلهتهم ليس بواصل إلى المقصود لنقصان ذويه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p183/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p183/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p183/r1.claim: The path belonging to God, who owns all things, implicitly criticizes polytheists for following another path; the discourse turns to threaten them with punishment for associating partners with Him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p183/r1.anchor: لما أفاد قوله : { إلى صراط العزيز الحميد الله الذي له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض } تعريضا بالمشركين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r1.claim: The discussion of the disconnected letters at the beginnings of sūras and the disagreements about them has already been given.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r1.anchor: تقدم القوم في الحروف المقطعة في أوائل السور والاختلاف في ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r2.claim: On the majority view that the opening letters are disjoint, kitāb is the predicate of an omitted “this is”; anzalnāhu is an adjective of kitāb.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r2.anchor: كتاب رفع على خبر ابتداء مضمر تقديره هذا كتاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r3.claim: Those who take the letters as names of the alphabet make kitāb the predicate of alif lām rā: these letters are a book revealed to the Prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r3.anchor: وأما من قال فيها، إنها كناية عن حروف المعجم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r4.speaker: القاضي ابن الطيب وأبو المعالي وغيرهما
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r4.claim: Al-Qāḍī Abū al-Ṭayyib, Abū al-Maʿālī, and others say revelation attaches not to God's eternal speech as an attribute, but to meanings God conveyed to Gabriel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r4.anchor: قال القاضي ابن الطيب وأبو المعالي وغيرهما: إن الإنزال لم يتعلق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r5.claim: The Prophet is credited with bringing people out because he participates through invitation and warning; the true act of creating and guiding belongs to God, and the wording honors the Prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r5.anchor: وقوله: لتخرج أسند الإخراج إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من حيث له فيه المشاركة بالدعاء والإنذار، وحقيقته إنما هي لله تعالى بالاختراع والهداية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r6.claim: “People” means all creation: the Qur'an and mass-transmitted reports establish that the Prophet was sent to the whole world, to the red and black.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r6.anchor: وعم الناس إذ هو مبعوث إلى جميع الخلق، ثبت ذلك بآيات القرآن التي اقترن بها ما نقل تواترا من دعوته العالم كله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r7.claim: Darkness is a metaphor for unbelief and light for faith.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r7.anchor: واستعير الظلمات للكفر، والنور للإيمان، تشبيها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r8.claim: By their Lord's permission means by His knowledge, decree, and enabling.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r8.anchor: وقوله: بإذن ربهم، أي بعلمه وقضائه به وتمكينه لهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r9.claim: The second ilā substitutes for the first: the path is the way leading to obedience, faith in God, and His mercy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r9.anchor: وإلى في قوله: إلى صراط بدل من الأولى في قوله: إلى النور أي إلى المحجة المؤدية إلى طاعة الله وللإيمان به ورحمته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r10.claim: The attributes fit the passage: might accompanies revelation and power, while deserved praise follows God's gift of guidance to the world.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r10.anchor: والعزيز الحميد صفتان لائقتان بهذا الموضع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r11.claim: Qur'anic verses and mass-transmitted reports establish the Prophet's worldwide mission; the Companions witnessed his invitation and transmitted it, making the fact certain.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r11.anchor: ومن بعثته إلى الأحمر والأسود علم الصحابة ذلك مشاهدة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r12.claim: God's deserved praise is linked to spreading the blessing of guidance throughout the world.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p321#2/r12.anchor: واستيجاب الحمد من جهة بث هذه النعم على العالم في نصب هدايتهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r1.claim: The disjoint letters alif-lām-rāʾ were explained earlier under Yūnus.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ( آلر ) قد سبق بيانه [ يونس 1 ]

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj understands kitāb as ‘this is a book,’ with the book referring to the Quran.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r2.anchor: وقوله ( كتاب ) قال الزجاج المعنى هذا كتاب والكتاب القرآن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r3.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r3.claim: Al-Awfi transmits from Ibn Abbas that darknesses mean unbelief and light means faith.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r3.anchor: أحدها أن الظلمات الكفر والنور الإيمان رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r4.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r4.claim: Mujahid and Qatada interpret darknesses as misguidance and light as guidance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r4.anchor: والثاني أن الظلمات الضلالة والنور الهدى قاله مجاهد وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r5.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r5.claim: Al-Mawardi gives doubt as the darknesses and certainty as the light.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r5.anchor: والثالث أن الظلمات الشك والنور اليقين ذكره الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r6.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r6.claim: Muqatil explains ‘by their Lord’s permission’ as by His command.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r7.speaker: أبو سليمان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r7.claim: Abu Sulayman takes the phrase to mean by their Lord’s enabling guidance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r7.anchor: والثاني بتوفيق ربهم قاله أبو سليمان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r8.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj reads it as permission itself: the Prophet teaches them what God has permitted him to teach.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r8.anchor: والثالث أنه الإذن نفسه فالمعنى بما أذن لك من تعليمهم قاله الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r9.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r9.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says repeating ilā magnifies the destination, as in Arabic ‘I sat toward Zayd, toward the intelligent, virtuous one.’
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r9.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري وهذا مثل قول العرب جلست إلى زيد إلى العاقل الفاضل وإنما تعاد إلى بمعنى التعظيم للأمر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r10.speaker: الشاعر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r10.claim: The poet's repeated ‘I called’ exemplifies repetition used to magnify the matter, as Ibn al-Anbari explains.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p343/r10.anchor: دعوت التي لو أن نفسي تطيعني لألقيتها من حبها وقضيت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p476#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p476#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p476#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr refers back to his earlier discussion of the disjointed letters at the beginnings of sūras.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p476#2/r1.anchor: قد تقدم الكلام على الحروف المقطعة في أوائل السور

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p476#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p476#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p476#2/r2.claim: The Book is the Qurʾan, the noblest book sent from heaven to the noblest messenger on earth, for all people, Arabs and non-Arabs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p476#2/r2.anchor: وهو القرآن العظيم، الذي هو أشرف كتاب أنزله الله من السماء، على أشرف رسول بعثه الله في الأرض، إلى جميع أهلها عربهم وعجمهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p476#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p476#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p476#2/r3.claim: The Qurʾan was given to bring people from misguidance and error to guidance and right direction, as in 2:257 and 57:9.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p476#2/r3.anchor: لتخرج الناس مما هم فيه من الضلال والغي إلى الهدى والرشد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p476#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p476#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p476#2/r4.claim: God guides through His messenger those for whom He has decreed guidance; the messenger was sent by God's command.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p476#2/r4.anchor: هو الهادي لمن قدر له الهداية على يدي رسوله المبعوث عن أمره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p476#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p476#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p476#2/r5.claim: The Mighty cannot be resisted or overcome and conquers all.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p476#2/r5.anchor: العزيز الذي لا يمانع ولا يغالب، بل هو القاهر لكل ما سواه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p476#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p476#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p476#2/r6.claim: The Praiseworthy is praised in every act, word, law, command, and prohibition, and is truthful in what He reports.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p476#2/r6.anchor: المحمود في جميع أفعاله وأقواله، وشرعه وأمره ونهيه، الصادق في خبره

JISHUMI:v5p3824/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن عامر
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r1.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, Nafiʿ, and Ibn ʿAmir raise Allah on a new clause, with its predicate following.
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر، ونافع، وابن عامر: الله الذي برفع اسم الله على الاستئناف

JISHUMI:v5p3824/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r2.speaker: الباقون
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r2.claim: The other readers put Allah in the genitive, linking it to al-Aziz al-Hamid.
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: بالكسر عطفا على قوله: العزيز الحميد

JISHUMI:v5p3824/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r3.claim: Abu ʿAmr explains the genitive through fronting and postponement: 'the path of Allah, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy.'
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r3.anchor: قال أبو عمرو: والخفض على التقديم والتأخير تقديره: صراط الله العزيز الحميد

JISHUMI:v5p3824/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r6.claim: Al-Aziz is invulnerable through power over affairs.
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r6.anchor: العزيز: الممتنع باقتداره على الأمور، عز يعز عزا وعزة فهو عزيز

JISHUMI:v5p3824/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r7.claim: Al-Hamid means praised in every state; hamadtu can mean I approved, while ahmadtu means I found it praiseworthy.
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r7.anchor: والحميد: فعيل من حمد يحمد حمدا فهو حميد؛ أي: محمود على كل حال

JISHUMI:v5p3824/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r8.claim: The sirat is a clear path and here means Islam.
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r8.anchor: والصراط: المنهاج البين، وهو ههنا دين الإسلام

JISHUMI:v5p3824/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r10.claim: Alif Lam Ra is a nominative subject with Kitab as predicate; alternatively, the implied phrase is 'this is a book sent down,' with Kitab as subject and anzalnahu its predicate, per al-Zajjaj.
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r10.anchor: (الر) محله رفع بالابتداء، وخبره كتاب، وقيل: تقديره: هذا كتاب أنزلناه

JISHUMI:v5p3824/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r11.claim: Al-Hamid is genitive as an adjective to al-Aziz, or nominative as a subject whose predicate is Allah.
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r11.anchor: والحميد خفض نعتا للعزيز، ويجوز في العربية رفعه على أنه ابتداء وخبره: الله

JISHUMI:v5p3824/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r13.speaker: الحسن والأصم وأبو علي
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r13.claim: One view identifies Alif Lam Ra as the sura's name; al-Hasan says the companions called such openings sura names and keys.
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r13.anchor: أنه اسم للسورة، عن الحسن، والأصم، وأبي علي

JISHUMI:v5p3824/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r14.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r14.claim: Abu Muslim says the letters signal the Quran's inimitability: it uses letters people know, yet they cannot produce its like.
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r14.anchor: أنه إشارة إلى أن هذه السورة مؤلفة من هذه الحروف، وبها تتكلمون، وعجزتم عن إتيان مثله

JISHUMI:v5p3824/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r15.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r15.claim: A third view says the opening letters are drawn from God's names and attributes.
JISHUMI:v5p3824/r15.anchor: أنها مأخوذة من أسمائه وصفاته تعالى

JISHUMI:v5p3825/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas interprets Alif Lam Ra as 'I am God who sees.'
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r1.anchor: (الر) أنا الله أرى، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v5p3825/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r2.claim: Kitab is the Quran, brought by Gabriel from God to His Messenger.
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r2.anchor: (كتاب) يعني القرآن (أنزلناه إليك) نزل به جبريل من الله تعالى إلى رسوله

JISHUMI:v5p3825/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says 'people' means Meccans, while another view says all creation; the author prefers all people because the Messenger was sent universally.
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r3.anchor: قيل: جميع الخلق، وقيل: أهل مكة، عن ابن عباس. والأول الوجه؛ لأنه مبعوث إلى الكافة

JISHUMI:v5p3825/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r4.claim: The verse figuratively attributes their exit from darkness to the Messenger because they leave when answering his call.
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r4.anchor: ونسب الإخراج إليه وإن كانوا خرجوا لأنهم خرجوا عند دعائه فجاز إضافته إليه

JISHUMI:v5p3825/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r5.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r5.claim: Qatada glosses darkness and light as misguidance and guidance.
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r5.anchor: من الضلالة إلى الهدى، عن قتادة

JISHUMI:v5p3825/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r6.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r6.claim: Abu ʿAli takes them as unbelief and faith: unbelief is the height of confusion, while faith illuminates guidance's paths.
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r6.anchor: من الكفر إلى الإيمان، وإنما شبه الكفر بالظلمة لأنها غاية ما يتحير به المرء

JISHUMI:v5p3825/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r7.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r7.claim: One interpretation of God's permission is His command.
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r7.anchor: بإذن ربهم قيل: بأمره، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v5p3825/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r8.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r8.claim: Al-Asamm says it means God's knowledge: He sent the Book with knowledge no one else could produce.
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r8.anchor: بعلمه، عن الأصم. يعني أنزل الكتاب بعلمه لا يقدر عليه غيره

JISHUMI:v5p3825/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r9.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r9.claim: Another gloss takes permission as God's kindness and facilitation.

JISHUMI:v5p3825/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r10.anchor: إلى صراط أي: طريق الله وهو الإسلام

JISHUMI:v5p3825/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r11.claim: God is powerful over what He wills and praised in every state; He is praised for His blessings and for all He does.
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r11.anchor: العزيز القادر على ما يشاء الحميد المحمود على كل حال

JISHUMI:v5p3825/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r12.claim: Calling God Praiseworthy signals that, despite His power, He does only what is good and worthy of praise.
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r12.anchor: وذكر الحميد تنبيها أنه تعالى وإن كان عزيزا قادرا على ما يشاء فلا يفعل إلا الحسن الحميد

JISHUMI:v5p3825/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r18.claim: The verse refutes determinism: if God created disbelief and faith, scripture could not bring people out of disbelief, nor could this act be attributed to the Messenger.
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r18.anchor: تدل الآية على بطلان مذهب الجبر من وجوه: أحدها: أن الكفر لو كان خلقا لله تعالى لم يصح إخراجهم

JISHUMI:v5p3825/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r19.claim: Deliverance through scripture requires people to reflect, infer, and believe, which presupposes their agency and choice.
JISHUMI:v5p3825/r19.anchor: أن الإخراج بالكتاب إنما يصح بأن يتدبر ويستدل ويؤمن، وذلك لا يصح إلا بعد أن يكون الفعل لهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r1.claim: “A book” here refers to the sura.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r1.anchor: { كتاب } هو كتاب ، يعني السورة . وقرىء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r2.claim: A variant reading has li-yukhrija al-nās (“so that he brings people out”).

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r3.claim: Darkness and light are metaphors for error and guidance.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r4.claim: By their Lord's permission means through His easing and facilitation, a metaphor from permission as the easing of a barrier; it is His grace and enabling guidance.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r4.anchor: بتسهيله وتيسيره ، مستعار من الإذن الذي هو تسهيل للحجاب ، وذلك ما يمنحهم من اللطف والتوفيق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r5.claim: The phrase can substitute for “to the light” with the preposition repeated, as in 7:75.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r5.anchor: بدل من قوله إلى النور بتكرير العامل ، كقوله : { للذين استضعفوا لمن ءامن منهم }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r6.claim: Alternatively, it begins a fresh explanation answering the question “to what light?”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون على وجه الاستئناف ، كأنه قيل : إلى أي نور ؟ فقيل : إلى صراط العزيز الحميد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r7.claim: The following description of those who fear God and do what they are commanded clarifies “the Mighty, the Praiseworthy,” which functions like a proper name for the uniquely worship-worthy God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r7.anchor: عطف بيان للعزيز الحميد ؛ لأنه جرى مجرى الأسماء الأعلام لغلبته واختصاصه بالمعبود الذي تحق له العبادة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r8.claim: A nominative reading construes the phrase as “He is God.”
