KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p505/r8.anchor: وقرىء بالرفع على : ( هو الله ) . الويل : نقيض الوأل

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p120/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p120/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p120/r1.claim: The Book sent down to Muhammad is the Qurʾan.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p120/r1.anchor: الر كتاب أنزلناه إليك } يعني القرآن

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p120/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p120/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p120/r2.claim: One explanation takes the movement from darkness to light as doubt to certainty.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p120/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p120/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p120/r3.claim: A second explanation takes it as movement from innovation to Sunna.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p120/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p120/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p120/r4.claim: A third explanation takes it as misguidance to guidance.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p120/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p120/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p120/r5.claim: A fourth explanation takes it as disbelief to faith.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p120/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p120/r6.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p120/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses God's permission as His command.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p120/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p120/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p120/r7.claim: A second gloss is by the knowledge of their Lord.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p120/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p120/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p120/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, through Muqsim, relates that some people believed in Jesus and others rejected him; when Muhammad was sent, those who had rejected Jesus believed in Muhammad, while those who had believed in Jesus rejected Muhammad, and the verse was revealed about them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p120/r8.anchor: فروى مقسم عن ابن عباس قال : كان قوم آمنوا بعيسى , وقوم كفروا به , فلما بعث محمد

MUQATIL:14:1/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:14:1/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:14:1/r1.claim: God sent the Book to Muhammad to bring people from darkness into light, meaning from idolatry to faith, by their Lord's command.
MUQATIL:14:1/r1.anchor: لتخرج الناس من الظلمات إلى النور

MUQATIL:14:1/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:14:1/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:14:1/r2.claim: The path is the religion; the Mighty is mighty in His dominion and the Praiseworthy is praised by His creatures for His command.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p222#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p222#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p222#2/r1.claim: Kitāb is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning this Book, namely the sūra; the clause anzalnāhu ilayka is an adjectival clause in the nominative.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p222#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ الر كتاب ﴾ هو خبر مبتدأ محذوف أي هذا كتاب يعنى السورة والجملة التي هي ﴿ أنزلناه إليك ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v2p222#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p222#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p222#2/r2.claim: The Prophet brings people from error to guidance by calling them.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p222#2/r2.anchor: ﴿ لتخرج الناس ﴾ بدعائك اياهم ﴿ من الظلمات إلى النور ﴾ من الضلالة إلى الهدى

NASAFI-FULL:v2p222#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p222#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p222#2/r3.claim: By their Lord's permission means by His enabling and easing their way, metaphorically likened to permission that opens a curtain.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p222#2/r3.anchor: ﴿ بإذن ربهم ﴾ بتيسيره وتسهيله مستعار من الاذن الذي هو تسهيل الحجاب

NASAFI-FULL:v2p222#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p222#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p222#2/r4.claim: The phrase to the path substitutes for the light, with the governing preposition repeated.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p222#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p222#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p222#2/r5.claim: Al-ʿAzīz is the one who prevails in retribution; al-Ḥamīd is praised for beneficence.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p222#2/r5.anchor: ﴿ العزيز ﴾ الغالب بالانتقام ﴿ الحميد ﴾ المحمود على الانعام

QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r1.claim: The commentator says the meaning of Alif Lam Ra has already been explained.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { الر كتاب أنزلناه إليك } تقدم معناه

QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r2.claim: The Prophet brings people out by means of the revealed Book, the Qurʾan, through calling them to it.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r2.anchor: أي بالكتاب، وهو القرآن، أي بدعائك إليه

QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r3.claim: The darknesses are disbelief, error, and ignorance; the light is faith and knowledge, with disbelief figuratively likened to darkness and Islam to light.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r3.anchor: أي من ظلمات الكفر والضلالة والجهل إلى نور الإيمان والعلم وهذا على التمثيل

QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r4.claim: Another explanation gives the parallel transitions as innovation to Sunnah and doubt to certainty; the commentator says the meaning is close.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r4.anchor: وقيل: من البدعة إلى السنة، ومن الشك إلى اليقين والمعنى متقارب

QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r5.claim: By their Lord’s permission means by His granting success and showing them kindness.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r6.claim: The preposition bi in “by their Lord’s permission” attaches to the verb “you bring out.”

QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r7.claim: The action is attributed to the Prophet because he calls, warns, and guides people.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r7.anchor: وأضيف الفعل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لأنه الداعي والمنذر الهادي

QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r8.claim: Al-Aziz and al-Hamid modify one and the same noun without a conjunction, like “I went to Zayd the wise, the noble.”
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r8.anchor: هو كقولك: خرجت إلى زيد العاقل الفاضل من غير واو، لأنهما شيء واحد

QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r9.claim: Al-Aziz is glossed as having no equal or likeness; another gloss is that no victor can overcome Him, or that He is inviolable in dominion and sovereignty.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r9.anchor: والله هو العزيز الذي لا مثل له ولا شبيه. وقيل: «العزيز» الذي لا يغلبه غالب. وقيل: «العزيز» المنيع في ملكه وسلطانه

QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r10.claim: Al-Hamid is praised by every tongue and glorified everywhere in every condition.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r10.anchor: «الحميد» أي المحمود بكل لسان، والممجد في كل مكان على كل حال

QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r11.speaker: مقسم عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r11.claim: Miqsam reports Ibn Abbas’s occasion of revelation: some people believed in Jesus and others rejected him; after Muhammad was sent, Jesus’s former rejecters believed Muhammad, while Jesus’s believers rejected him.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:1/r11.anchor: وروى مقسم عن ابن عباس قال: كان قوم آمنوا بعيسى ابن مريم، وقوم كفروا به

QASHANI:14:1-2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:14:1-2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:14:1-2/r1.claim: The Book leads people from multiplicity to unity, or from the darkness of their created nature to primordial light, or from veils of acts and attributes to the light of the essence.
QASHANI:14:1-2/r1.anchor: من ظلمات الكثرة إلى نور الوحدة

QASHANI:14:1-2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:14:1-2/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:14:1-2/r2.claim: The Lord’s permission is His gift of readiness through the most holy effusion and His preparation of the causes by which the light becomes actual; without this, no one could lead people out.
QASHANI:14:1-2/r2.anchor: إذ الإذن منه هبة الاستعداد وتهيئة الأسباب

QASHANI:14:1-2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:14:1-2/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:14:1-2/r3.claim: On the unity reading, the path is of the Mighty, who overcomes multiplicity’s darkness by unity’s light, and the Praiseworthy, perfect in essence.
QASHANI:14:1-2/r3.anchor: القوي الذي يقهر ظلمات الكثرة بنور وحدته

QASHANI:14:1-2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:14:1-2/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:14:1-2/r4.claim: On the primordial-nature reading, the Mighty overcomes the soul’s qualities through heart-light, and the Praiseworthy grants virtues and knowledge when nature is purified.
QASHANI:14:1-2/r4.anchor: الذي يقهر صفات النفس بنور القلب { الحميد } الذي يهب نعم الفضائل والعلوم عند صفاء الفطرة

QASHANI:14:1-2/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:14:1-2/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:14:1-2/r5.claim: On the essence reading, the Mighty’s effulgence overpowers attribute-lights and annihilates creatures through His identity; the Praiseworthy gives lasting, perfect existence after their deficient vices pass away.
QASHANI:14:1-2/r5.anchor: الذي يقهر بسبحات ذاته أنوار صفاته ويفنى بحقيقة هويته جميع مخلوقاته الحميد الذي يهب الوجود الباقي الكامل بعد فناء الرذائل الناقص بوجود ذاته وجمال وجهه

RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r1.claim: The chapter of Ibrahim has fifty-two verses and is Meccan; whether it is Meccan or Medinan rests on solitary reports and matters chiefly when legal material could involve abrogation.

RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r2.claim: Alif Lām Rā is the subject, kitāb its predicate, and anzalnāhu ilayka an adjective of that predicate; the phrase identifies a named surah as a book sent to the Prophet for a purpose.
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r2.anchor: وقوله : { الر كتاب } معناه أن السورة المسماة بالر كتاب أنزلناه إليك لغرض كذا وكذا

RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r3.claim: The Mu'tazilites argue that what is sent down cannot be eternal.
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r3.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : النازل والمنزل لا يكون قديما

RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r4.claim: Razi replies that the thing described as sent down is the Qur'an's letters, which are originated and whose originated status is undisputed.
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r4.anchor: وجوابنا : أن الموصوف بالنازل والمنزل هو هذه الحروف وهي محدثة بلا نزاع

RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r5.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r5.claim: The Mu'tazilites read the lām as purposive: God sent the book to guide people, which they take to show that divine acts and rulings are directed toward benefits.
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r5.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : اللام في قوله : { لتخرج الناس } لام الغرض والحكمة

RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r6.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r6.claim: Razi's school argues that acting for a further purpose would imply God cannot achieve it without an intermediary; since that is impossible, apparent wording that suggests causal purposes must be reinterpreted.
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r6.anchor: أجاب أصحابنا عنه بأن من فعل فعلا لأجل شيء آخر فهذا إنما يفعله لو كان عاجزا عن تحصيل هذا المقصود

RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r7.claim: Kufr is likened to darkness because it is the farthest point of confusion about guidance; faith is light because it most fully clarifies the path.
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r7.anchor: إنما شبه الكفر بالظلمات لأنه نهاية ما يتحير الرجل فيه عن طريق الهداية وشبه الإيمان بالنور

RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r8.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r8.claim: The Qadi argues that if God created unbelief in an unbeliever, it would make no sense for the Prophet to remove that person from it through the book.
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r8.anchor: قال القاضي : هذه الآية فيها دلالة على إبطال القول بالجبر

RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r9.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r9.claim: The Qadi argues that attributing guidance to the Messenger conflicts with God creating unbelief; an unbeliever could answer that if God creates future disbelief, the Messenger cannot remove it, and if not, no removal by him is needed.
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r9.anchor: وثانيها : أنه تعالى أضاف الإخراج من الظلمات إلى النور إلى الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r10.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r10.claim: The Qadi says the Prophet recites the book so people reason to God's knowledge, power, and wisdom, recognize the Qur'an's miraculous character and his truthfulness, then accept its laws; this requires acts they perform by choice.
RAZI-FULL:v19p57/r10.anchor: وثالثها : أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما يخرجهم من الكفر بالكتاب بأن يتلوه عليهم ليتدبروه

RAZI-FULL:v19p58/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p58/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p58/r1.claim: An act cannot issue when motives equally favor action and inaction; if one side prevails, its source either raises the same regress or is God, the first effective cause.
RAZI-FULL:v19p58/r1.anchor: الفعل الصادر من العبد إما أن يصدر عنه حال استواء الداعي إلى الفعل والترك أو حال رجحان أحد الطرفين على الآخر

RAZI-FULL:v19p58/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p58/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p58/r2.claim: The Ashʿarite argument reads God's permission as will and creation: it cannot mean command or knowledge, since neither causes the transition from error to guidance.
RAZI-FULL:v19p58/r2.anchor: ولما بطل هذان القسمان لم يبق إلا أن يكون المراد من الإذن المشيئة والتخليق

RAZI-FULL:v19p58/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p58/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p58/r3.claim: An appeal to divine لطف does not evade the argument: if it does not tip action over inaction it cannot cause the result, and if it does, it necessitates the result.
RAZI-FULL:v19p58/r3.anchor: المراد بالإذن إما أن يكون أمرا يقتضي ترجيح جانب الوجود على جانب العدم أو لا يقتضي ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r1.speaker: القائلون
RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r1.claim: Those who require instruction from a prophet and imam for knowledge of God infer that the Messenger's role in bringing people from disbelief to faith makes such teaching indispensable.
RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r1.anchor: القائلون بأن معرفة الله تعالى لا يمكن تحصيلها إلا من تعليم الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم والإمام

RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r2.claim: Razi answers that the Messenger only alerts people; knowledge itself is obtained through proof.
RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r2.anchor: أن الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم يكون كالمنبه ، وأما المعرفة فهي إنما تحصل بالدليل

RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r3.claim: The plural darknesses and singular light indicate many paths of ignorance and disbelief, while knowledge, faith, and guidance have one path.
RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r3.anchor: عبر عن الجهل والكفر بالظلمات وهي صيغة جمع وعبر عن الإيمان والهداية بالنور وهو لفظ مفرد

RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r4.claim: One parsing treats “to the path” as an apposition to “to the light,” with the governing preposition repeated; Razi compares Qur'an 7:75.
RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r4.anchor: إلى النور بتكرير العامل كقوله : { للذين استضعفوا لمن ءامن منهم }

RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r5.claim: Alternatively, “to the path of the Mighty, Praiseworthy” begins a fresh sentence answering the implied question, “To which light?”
RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r5.anchor: يجوز أن يكون على وجه الاستئناف كأنه قيل : إلى أي نور فقيل : { إلى صراط العزيز الحميد }

RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r6.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r6.claim: The Muʿtazila argue that right action requires an agent able to do all things, knowing all things, and independent of every need; otherwise incapacity, ignorance, or need could prompt evil.
RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r6.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : الفاعل إنما يكون آتيا بالصواب والصلاح ، تاركا للقبيح

RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r7.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r7.claim: In their reading, “Mighty” signals complete power and “Praiseworthy” God's deserving praise in all acts, which entails knowledge and freedom from need.
RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r7.anchor: فقوله : { العزيز } إشارة إلى كمال القدرة ، وقوله : { الحميد } إشارة إلى كونه مستحقا للحمد

RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r8.claim: The path is exalted and straight because it belongs to the deity who is Mighty and Praiseworthy.
RAZI-FULL:v19p59/r8.anchor: صراطا مستقيما للإله الموصوف بكونه عزيزا حميدا

QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r1.claim: Qushayri glosses the invocation as being by God and links it to the knowers’ illumination and lovers’ burning.
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r1.anchor: فقلوب العارفين بالله أشراقها ، وقولب الوالهين بالله احتراقها

QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r2.claim: The knowers’ hearts are illuminated by God, while the ecstatic lovers’ hearts burn through God; the latter long for the sight of the Mighty.
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r2.anchor: فقلوب العارفين بالله أشراقها ، وقولب الوالهين بالله احتراقها

QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r3.speaker: أصحاب الوصول
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r3.claim: Those who have arrived say ‘by God’; among seekers, some consequently attain arrival.
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r3.anchor: وأصحاب الوصول قالوا : بالله . . . فوصل من الطالبين من وصل

QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r4.claim: The opening disconnected letters serve as an oath affirming that this is a book sent down to the Prophet.
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r4.anchor: أقسم بهذه الحروف : إنه لكتاب أنزل إليك

QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r5.claim: The Quran takes people from ignorance’s darkness to knowledge’s light.
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r5.anchor: من ظلمات الجهل إلى نور العلم

QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r6.claim: It takes people from doubt to certainty.
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r6.anchor: ومن ظلمات الشك إلى نور اليقين

QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r7.claim: It takes people from worldly planning to the spaciousness of witnessing the divine decree.
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r7.anchor: ومن ظلمات التدبير إلى فضاء شهود التقدير

QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r8.claim: It takes people from religious innovation to following the revealed path.
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r8.anchor: ومن ظلمات الابتداع إلى نور الاتباع

QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r9.claim: It takes people from the ego’s claims to the heart’s gnoses.
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r9.anchor: ومن ظلمات دعاوى النفس إلى نور معارف القلب

QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r10.claim: It takes people from separation to unitive gathering.
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r10.anchor: ومن ظلمات التفرقة إلى نور الجمع

QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r11.claim: This passage occurs by God’s permission, will, choice, and prior decree.
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r11.anchor: بإذن ربهم - وبإرادته ومشيئته ، وسابق حكمه وقضائه

QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r12.claim: The path of the Mighty and Praiseworthy is the path of divine mercy, tawhid, and the signs of divine uniqueness.
QUSHAYRI:v2p115/r12.anchor: إلى صراط رحمته ، وهو نهج التوحيد وشواهد التفريد

STUDYQURAN:14:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:1/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:1/r1.claim: The separated letters are discussed at 2:1.

STUDYQURAN:14:1/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:1/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:1/r2.claim: The Book refers to the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:14:1/r2.anchor: A Book refers to the Quran (Bg, My, Ṭ; cf. 13:1).

STUDYQURAN:14:1/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:1/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:1/r3.claim: By calling people to the Quran, the Prophet leads them from disbelief, ignorance, and doubt to guidance, knowledge, and certainty.
STUDYQURAN:14:1/r3.anchor: By means of calling people to the Quran (Q), the Prophet brings human beings out of darkness into light, that is, from the darkness of disbelief, ignorance, and doubt

STUDYQURAN:14:1/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:1/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:1/r4.claim: A similar image of bringing people from darkness to light appears at 14:5 and 65:11; elsewhere God is the subject of this image.
STUDYQURAN:14:1/r4.anchor: Elsewhere in the Quran God is the subject of similar phrases in which He is said to bring forth mankind out of darkness into light

STUDYQURAN:14:1/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:1/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:1/r5.claim: By their Lord's leave refers to God's kindness in bestowing grace and granting people success in guidance.
STUDYQURAN:14:1/r5.anchor: By the leave of their Lord refers to God’s Kindness in bestowing grace upon people and granting them success in being guided out of darkness into light

STUDYQURAN:14:1/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:1/r6.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:14:1/r6.claim: The path may mean the light mentioned here or Islam itself.
STUDYQURAN:14:1/r6.anchor: The path can refer to being led to the light mentioned in this verse (Aj), or to Islam itself (AF).

STUDYQURAN:14:1/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:1/r7.speaker: al-Qummī
STUDYQURAN:14:1/r7.claim: Al-Qummī interprets the path as the leadership of the Twelve Imams.
STUDYQURAN:14:1/r7.anchor: Qummī, the path refers to the leadership of the Twelve Imams.

STUDYQURAN:14:1/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:1/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:1/r8.claim: Mighty signifies God's perfect Power, while Praised means that He deserves praise in all that He does.
STUDYQURAN:14:1/r8.anchor: The name Mighty refers to the perfection of God’s Power, whereas the name Praised means that God is deserving of praise in all that He does (R)

SULAMI:v1p340/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p340/r1.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p340/r1.claim: The revelation is a special covenant that recounts the destruction of earlier peoples and the salvation of Muhammad's community.
SULAMI:v1p340/r1.anchor: قال جعفر : عهد خصصت به فيه بيان هلاك سالف الأمم ونجاة أمتك

SULAMI:v1p340/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p340/r2.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p340/r2.claim: The revelation brings people from disbelief to faith, innovation to the lights of Sunna, and darkness of the selves to the lights of hearts.
SULAMI:v1p340/r2.anchor: قال جعفر : عهد خصصت به فيه بيان هلاك سالف الأمم ونجاة أمتك ، أنزلناه إليك لتخرجهم به من ظلمات الكفر إلى نور الإيمان ،

SULAMI:v1p340/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p340/r3.speaker: أبو بكر
SULAMI:v1p340/r3.claim: The darkness is conjecture and the light is reality.
SULAMI:v1p340/r3.anchor: قال أبو بكر : من ظلمات الظن إلى أنوار الحقيقة

SULAMI:v1p340/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p340/r4.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v1p340/r4.claim: The darkness is shirk and the light is guidance.
SULAMI:v1p340/r4.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : من ظلمات الشرك إلى أنوار الهدى

SULAMI:v1p340/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p340/r5.speaker: أبو حفص
SULAMI:v1p340/r5.claim: Darkness means seeing one's own actions; light means seeing divine grace.
SULAMI:v1p340/r5.anchor: قال أبو حفص : الظلمة رؤية الفعل والنور رؤية الفضل

TAB-FULL:v13p588#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p588#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p588#2/r1.claim: The book revealed to Muḥammad is the Qurʾān.
TAB-FULL:v13p588#2/r1.anchor: معناه: هذا كتاب أنزلناه إليك يا محمد، يعني القرآن {لتخرج الناس من الظلمات إلى النور} [إبراهيم: 1]

TAB-FULL:v13p588#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p588#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p588#2/r2.claim: Through the Qurʾān, Muḥammad guides people from the darkness of error and unbelief to the light of faith, showing the ignorant the paths of right guidance.
TAB-FULL:v13p588#2/r2.anchor: لتهديهم به من ظلمات الضلالة والكفر إلى نور الإيمان وضيائه

TAB-FULL:v13p589/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p589/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p589/r1.claim: By their Lord's permission means by His granting them success and showing them gracious care.
TAB-FULL:v13p589/r1.anchor: إلى النور بإذن ربهم لهم بذلك إلى نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم،

TAB-FULL:v13p589/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p589/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p589/r2.claim: God guides creation and grants faith to whom He wills, while the Prophet calls people and explains their obligations; this supports the affirmationists' account of human acts as acquisition created and governed by God, against the Qadariyya.
TAB-FULL:v13p589/r2.anchor: صحة قول أهل الإثبات الذين أضافوا أفعال العباد إليهم كسبا، وإلى الله جل ثناؤه إنشاء وتدبيرا، وفساد قول أهل القدر

TAB-FULL:v13p589/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p589/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p589/r3.claim: Qatāda glosses the movement from darkness to light as movement from error to guidance.
TAB-FULL:v13p589/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {لتخرج الناس من الظلمات إلى النور} [إبراهيم: 1] : «أي من الضلالة إلى الهدى»

TABATABAI:14:1/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:1/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:1/r1.claim: The sūra presents the revealed Qur'an as the sign of the Prophet's mission: through it he brings people from darkness to light and guides them to God's path.
TABATABAI:14:1/r1.anchor: تصف القرآن النازل على النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم من حيث إنه آية رسالته يخرج به الناس من الظلمات إلى النور ويهديهم إلى صراط الله سبحانه

TABATABAI:14:1/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:1/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:1/r2.claim: Al-ʿAzīz is unconquered and free of need; al-Ḥamīd is beautiful in action and bestows favors on people.
TABATABAI:14:1/r2.anchor: أي غالب غير مغلوب وغني غير محتاج إلى الناس وجميل في فعله منعم عليهم

TABATABAI:14:1/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:1/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:1/r3.claim: Because the Benefactor is mighty, independent, and praiseworthy in His acts, people should answer His call, accept it for their happiness, and fear His displeasure and severe punishment; He can replace earlier ungrateful peoples.
TABATABAI:14:1/r3.anchor: وإذا كان المنعم غالبا غنيا حميد الأفعال كان على المنعم عليهم أن يجيبوا دعوته ويلبوا نداءه حتى يسعدوا بما أفاض عليهم من النعم

TABATABAI:14:1/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:1/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:1/r4.claim: The sūra's conclusion that the message is a warning to all people and proclaims one God closes the argument begun at its opening; the signs of heaven and earth show that all blessing belongs to Him.
TABATABAI:14:1/r4.anchor: إذ يقول عز من قائل { هذا بلاغ للناس ولينذروا به وليعلموا أنما هو إله واحد

TABATABAI:14:1/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:1/r5.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
TABATABAI:14:1/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, and Qatāda regard the sūra as Meccan except for two verses said to concern the polytheists killed at Badr.
TABATABAI:14:1/r5.anchor: ونسب إلى ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة أنها مكية إلا آيتين منها نزلتا في قتلى بدر من المشركين

TABATABAI:14:1/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:1/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:1/r7.claim: He construes the opening as “This is a Book We sent down to you,” with the sentence serving as the predicate of an omitted subject.
TABATABAI:14:1/r7.anchor: أي هذا كتاب أنزلناه إليك، فهو خبر لمبتدأ محذوف على ما يعطيه السياق

TABATABAI:14:1#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:1#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:1#2/r1.claim: “People” means humanity generally, not only the Prophet's own people or believers, since the verse gives no verbal basis for restricting its scope.
TABATABAI:14:1#2/r1.anchor: قل يا أيها الناس إني رسول الله إليكم جميعا

TABATABAI:14:1#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:1#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:1#2/r2.claim: The Prophet is named as the apparent means by which people leave darkness: believers' faith traces to his invitation directly or through intermediaries, without making him an independent source of guidance.
TABATABAI:14:1#2/r2.anchor: أحد الأسباب الظاهرية لذلك وإليه ينتهي إيمان المؤمنين بدعوته

TABATABAI:14:1#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:1#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:1#2/r3.claim: The denial in 28:56 concerns the Prophet's independent, original guidance; it does not deny guidance by mediation and God's permission, as 42:52 confirms.
TABATABAI:14:1#2/r3.anchor: فإن الآية إنما تنفي أصالته صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في الهداية واستقلاله فيها من غير أن تنفي عنه مطلق الهداية

TABATABAI:14:1#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:1#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:1#2/r4.claim: Darkness and light signify misguidance and guidance; darkness is plural because divergent desires fragment error, while truth and guidance are one.
TABATABAI:14:1#2/r4.anchor: والمراد بالظلمات والنور الضلال والهدى، وقد تكرر في كلامه تعالى

TABATABAI:14:1#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:1#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:1#2/r5.claim: The lām in “so that you may bring out” marks purpose, not eventual consequence: a consequence reading would imply that all people become believers, which is false.
TABATABAI:14:1#2/r5.anchor: واللام في قوله { لتخرج الناس } الخ، لام الغرض بناء على عموم الناس كما هو ظاهر الآية

TABATABAI:14:1#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:1#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:14:1#2/r6.claim: Some object that divine guidance and delivery to perfection require people's preparedness, so universal grace can reach its outcome only to that extent.
TABATABAI:14:1#2/r6.anchor: وأما ما اعترض عليه بعضهم أن التربية الإلهية بإخراج الناس من الظلمات إلى النور وإيصالهم إلى السعادة والكمال مشروطة بالتهيؤ والاستعداد

TABATABAI:14:1#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:1#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:1#2/r7.claim: The objection requires restricting “people,” conceding that the lām is not a consequence marker; instead, the verse states a legislative aim, the welfare God intends through commands, messengers, and scripture, including guidance, purification, and salvation.
TABATABAI:14:1#2/r7.anchor: لكن الذي يجب أن يعلم أن هذا الغرض غرض تشريعي معناه أن للحكم غاية مقصودة وهي المصلحة التي يستعقبها

TABRISI:14:1-2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:1-2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:1-2/r8.claim: Al-ʿAzīz is able to do all things and invulnerable by His power; al-Ḥamīd is praised in every circumstance.
TABRISI:14:1-2/r8.anchor: العزيز القادر على الأشياء الممتنع بقدرته

TABRISI:14:1-2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:1-2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:1-2/r9.claim: Istiḥbāb is seeking to gain love; love can mean willing benefits for the beloved or natural inclination, desire, or appetite, while بغية and ابتغاء mean seeking.
TABRISI:14:1-2/r9.anchor: والاستحباب طلب محبة الشيء بالتعرض لها

TABRISI:14:1-2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:1-2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:1-2/r10.claim: The author directs readers to his earlier discussion in the opening of al-Baqara for meanings and disagreements about the disjoined letters.

TABRISI:14:1-2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:1-2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:1-2/r11.claim: The Book is the Qurʾān, brought from God by Gabriel to Muhammad; it is neither sorcery nor poetry.
TABRISI:14:1-2/r11.anchor: نزل به جبرائيل ع من عند الله تعالى

TABRISI:14:1-2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:1-2/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:1-2/r12.claim: The Qurʾān is sent so that all people may be led from misguidance and disbelief to guidance and faith, by God’s authorization and command.
TABRISI:14:1-2/r12.anchor: من الضلالة إلى الهدى ومن الكفر إلى الإيمان

TABRISI:14:1-2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:1-2/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:1-2/r13.claim: The purpose-marking lām shows that God wills faith for all accountable people; it cannot be a lām of consequence, since that would imply everyone became a believer.
TABRISI:14:1-2/r13.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على أنه سبحانه يريد الإيمان من جميع المكلفين

TABRISI:14:1-2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:1-2/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:1-2/r14.claim: The light leads to God’s path and knowledge of Him; He is invincible in sovereignty and praised for His acts and blessings to servants.
TABRISI:14:1-2/r14.anchor: أي يخرجهم من ظلمات الكفر إلى طريق الله المؤدي إلى معرفة الله

THALABI:v5p305/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p305/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p305/r1.claim: He begins the book's predication with kitāb, construing the opening as This is a book We sent down to you, Muhammad.
THALABI:v5p305/r1.anchor: الر ابتدأ كتاب خبره وإن قلت هذا كتاب أنزلناه إليك يا محمد

THALABI:v5p305/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p305/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p305/r2.claim: The Quran calls people from error and ignorance to knowledge and faith by God's enabling and gracious guidance, onto the path of the Mighty, Praiseworthy.
THALABI:v5p305/r2.anchor: لتخرج الناس لتدعوهم [إليه] من الظلمات الضلالة والجهالة إلى النور العلم والإيمان بإذن ربهم

THALABI:v5p305/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p305/r3.speaker: أهل المدينة والشام
THALABI:v5p305/r3.claim: Medinan and Syrian readers pronounce Allāh with nominative hāʾ as a new sentence, with alladhī as its predicate.

THALABI:v5p305/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p305/r4.speaker: الآخرون
THALABI:v5p305/r4.claim: The other readers pronounce Allāh in the genitive as an adjective of al-ʿAzīz al-Ḥamīd.
THALABI:v5p305/r4.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون: بالخفض نعتا ل العزيز الحميد

THALABI:v5p305/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p305/r5.speaker: أبو عمر
THALABI:v5p305/r5.claim: Abu Amr explains the genitive by fronting and postponement: the meaning is the path of God, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, God to whom all belongs.
THALABI:v5p305/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عمر: بالخفض على التقديم والتأخير، مجازه: إلى صراط الله العزيز الحميد

THALABI:v5p305/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p305/r6.speaker: يعقوب بن إسحاق الحضرمي
THALABI:v5p305/r6.claim: Yaqub raises Allāh when pausing after al-Ḥamīd and reads it in the genitive when continuing as an adjective.
THALABI:v5p305/r6.anchor: وكان يعقوب بن إسحاق الحضرمي إذا وقف على الحميد رفع قوله الله وإذا وصل خفض على النعت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r1.speaker: أبو صالح وعطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r1.claim: In reports from Abu Salih and Ata, the disjoined letters mean I am God, the Merciful.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r1.anchor: وقال في رواية أبي صالح وعطاء: أنا الله الرحمن (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r2.claim: Kitab is nominative as the predicate of an understood subject: this is a Book We sent down to you.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r2.anchor: وعلى هذا التفسير # قوله: {كتاب} مرفوع على خبر الابتداء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r3.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r3.claim: The author of al-Nazm calls alif lam ra a name for the set of alphabetic letters; the Book is composed of these letters, so the phrase means these letters are a Book sent down.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r3.anchor: وقال صاحب النظم (¬2): {الر} اسم موضوع لجماعة الحروف المعجمة (¬3)، فعلى هذا {كتاب} موضوع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r4.claim: Anzalnahu ilayka qualifies kitab, like saying Zayd is a man I sent to you.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r4.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {أنزلناه إليك} من صفة الكتاب، ومثل هذا من الكلام: زيد رجل أنفذته إليك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r5.claim: The purpose clause li-tukhrija is attached to the sending: God sent the Book for the purpose of bringing people out.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r5.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {لتخرج الناس} سبب لقوله {أنزلناه إليك}، فاللام في {لتخرج} معلق بالإنزال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the movement from darkness to light as movement from polytheism to faith.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد من الشرك إلى الإيمان (¬6)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r7.claim: Abu Ishaq says disbelief is compared to darkness because it is unclear, while faith is clear and luminous like light.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p393#3/r7.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: شبه الكفر بالظلمات لأنه غير # بين، الإيمان بين نير، فمثل بالنور (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p395/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p395/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p395/r1.claim: Abu Ishaq connects bi-idhn to li-tukhrija: the Prophet brings people out with God's permission, that is, by God's authorization to teach them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p395/r1.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون {بإذن ربهم}: لا (¬2) يهتدي مهتد إلا بإذن الله ومشيئته (¬3)، هذا كله كلام أبي إسحاق (¬4)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p395/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p395/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p395/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas takes God's permission as His decree: no one is guided except by God's permission and will.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p395/r2.anchor: والقول الثاني قول ابن عباس؛ لأنه قال: يريد بقضاء ربهم (¬5)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p395/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p395/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p395/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbari explains the lack of a conjunction: the second path is the previously mentioned light, and the repeated ila attaches it semantically to the first phrase.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p395/r3.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: إنما لم يدخل حرف العطف في {إلى صراط} (¬6) لأنه أريد بهذا الصراط: النور المذكور قبله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p395/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p395/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p395/r4.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says the repeated ila magnifies the description; the path of the Mighty, Praiseworthy is praise and description of the light, which is Islam.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p395/r4.anchor: وإنما تعاد (إلى) لمعنى (¬10) التفخيم والتعظيم، فالنور: هو الإسلام، وصراط العزيز الحميد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p395/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p395/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p395/r5.claim: Abu Ishaq says the phrase then clarifies what the light is: the path of the Mighty, Praiseworthy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p395/r5.anchor: وهذا معنى قول أبي # إسحاق: ثم بين ما النور فقال: {إلى صراط العزيز الحميد} (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p396#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p396#3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p396#3/r1.claim: In the genitive construction, Allah is analyzed as an apposition to al-Hamid rather than its adjective, because Allah functions as a proper name through frequent use.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p396#3/r1.anchor: ومن خفض (¬5) جعله بدلا من {الحميد} ولم يكن صفة؛ لأن اسم الله صار كالعلم (¬6)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p396#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p396#3/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p396#3/r2.claim: Although Allah can descriptively mean the One deserving worship, a quality can become a proper name through common use; the poet's al-Nabigha illustrates this shift.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p396#3/r2.anchor: على # معنى أن العبادة تجب له، وقد يغلب ما أصله الصفة فيصير بمنزلة العلم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p396#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p396#3/r3.speaker: الشاعر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p396#3/r3.claim: The cited line calls the poet al-Nabigha without the definite article, illustrating how a descriptive epithet can become a proper name.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p396#3/r3.anchor: كقول الشاعر (¬1): ونابغة الجعدي بالرمل بيته ... عليه صفيح من تراب وجندل (¬2)

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:1/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:1/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:1/r1.claim: The disjoined letters mean, “I am God; I see.”

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:1/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:1/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:1/r2.claim: The Book was sent to Muhammad to lead people from associationism to faith by God's permission and decree, since only God can permit guidance.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:1/r2.anchor: { كتاب أنزلناه إليك لتخرج الناس من الظلمات إلى النور } من الشرك إلى الإيمان { بإذن ربهم } بقضاء ربهم؛ لأنه لا يهتدي مهتد إلا بإذن الله سبحانه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:1/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:1/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:1/r3.claim: The path of the Mighty and Praiseworthy identifies the light to which the Book guides.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:1/r3.anchor: ثم بين ما ذلك النور فقال: { إلى صراط العزيز الحميد }.

ELMALILI:14:1-3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:14:1-3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:14:1-3/r1.claim: The disjoined letters have parallels since Sūrat Yūnus; their ultimate intended meaning is known to God.
ELMALILI:14:1-3/r1.anchor: Sûre-i Yûnus’tan beri geçen nazîrlerine bak. االله أَعْلَمُ بِمُرَادِهِ

ELMALILI:14:1-3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:14:1-3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:14:1-3/r2.claim: Elmalılı reads these distinct letters as a sign of unity and straightness, with Alif assisting all letters and Lām and Rā rolling through recitation into the multiplicity of address.
ELMALILI:14:1-3/r2.anchor: bâtından çıkıp her harfe imdad eden elif gibi tevhid ve istikāmet delîli olarak tecellî eden

ELMALILI:14:1-3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:14:1-3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:14:1-3/r3.claim: God, in majestic power, sent this magnificent book down to Muhammad so he could lead people from darkness into light by their Lord's permission.
ELMALILI:14:1-3/r3.anchor: onu sana şân-ı azametimizle Biz indirdik. İndirdik ki

ELMALILI:14:1-3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:14:1-3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:14:1-3/r4.claim: The mission is universal: rescue people from ignorance, sensuality, disbelief, misguidance, false aims, and idols, guiding them by faith to God's religion and law.
ELMALILI:14:1-3/r4.anchor: ale’l-umûm insanları dalâlet ve sefaletten kurtarıp nûr-i iman ile izzet ü hamd yoluna

ELMALILI:14:1-3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:14:1-3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:14:1-3/r5.claim: The Prophet does not guide people by independent power or will; guidance comes with the permission and enabling of the Lord of all worlds.
ELMALILI:14:1-3/r5.anchor: Fakat kendi kudret ve iradenle değil, hepsinin Rabbi olan O Rabbü’l-âlemî’nin izn ü tevfîkiyle

ELMALILI:14:1-3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:14:1-3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:14:1-3/r6.claim: God is wholly mighty and worthy of praise; those who take refuge in His protection are honored by His might and bounty.
ELMALILI:14:1-3/r6.anchor: bütün izzet ve kudret kendisinin, bütün hamd ü senâ kendisine mahsus olan

ELMALILI:14:1-3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:14:1-3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:14:1-3/r14.claim: Elmalılı anticipates their objection that a universal messenger would not receive an Arabic book, since no earlier prophet had received one and this would oppose God's established custom.
ELMALILI:14:1-3/r14.anchor: “sen bütün insanlara mürsel bir resul olsa idin bu kitap Arapça mı olurdu? Hem bu hangi peygamberde görülmüş?

MAJAZ:v1p335/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p335/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p335/r1.claim: Alif-lām-rā is unvoweled like the initials opening other sūras; these are letter names, and their semantic role is that of a sūra’s opening.
MAJAZ:v1p335/r1.anchor: الر» (1) ساكن لأنه جرى مجرى فواتح سائر السور اللواتى مجازهن مجاز حروف التهجي

MAJAZ:v1p335/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p335/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p335/r2.claim: The phrase may begin a new sentence or omit a pronoun, as in ‘this is a book We sent down’; compare the explicit wording in 2:1.
MAJAZ:v1p335/r2.anchor: كتاب أنزلناه إليك» مجازه مستأنف أو مختصر فيه ضمير كقولك: هذا كتاب أنزلناه إليك، وفى آية أخرى: «الم ذلك الكتاب» (2/ 1)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r1.claim: The detached opening letters are called huruf al-muqatta'a.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r1.anchor: Bazı sûrelerin başında bulunan bu harflere “hurûf-i mukattaa” denir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r2.claim: Openings with these letters are usually followed by mention of the Book, verses, or revelation; this passage follows that pattern.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r2.anchor: Bu harflerden sonra genellikle kitaptan, âyetlerden veya vahiyden söz edilir. Burada da aynı üslûp kullanılmıştır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r3.claim: The Book sent down to the Prophet is the Quran.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r3.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’e indirilen kitaptan maksat Kur’an’dır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r4.claim: God calls ignorance, unbelief, and false belief darkness, and knowledge, faith, and guidance light.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r4.anchor: Allah Teâlâ cehalet, inkâr, bâtıl inanç gibi durumları zulumât (karanlık); bilgi, iman, hidayet gibi hasletleri de nûr (aydınlık) olarak nitelemiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r5.claim: “By their Lord's leave” indicates that the Prophet fulfills this task by God's command and will, not on his own initiative.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r5.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in bu görevi kendiliğinden değil, Allah’ın emri ve iradesiyle yerine getirdiğine işaret eder.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r6.speaker: bir anlayış
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r6.claim: Another reading takes the phrase to mean that the Prophet's role is only to convey the message, while guidance depends on God's permission and will.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r6.anchor: Bir anlayışa göre de bu ifade peygamberin görevinin sadece tebliğ etmek olduğunu; hidayete erdirmenin ise Allah’ın izin ve iradesine bağlı bulunduğunu gösterir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r7.claim: God governs the heavens and earth and guides those who seek the right path; He leaves idolaters who wrongly choose created beings to wander and warns them of severe punishment.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:1/r7.anchor: Göklerin ve yerin mülkiyet ve yönetimini elinde bulunduran Allah, doğru yolu bulmak isteyenleri doğru yola iletir

BURHAN:v3p442/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p442/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p442/r10.claim: The Qur'an's uses of darkness and light are all metaphorical.
BURHAN:v3p442/r10.anchor: وكل ما في القرآن من الظلمات والنور مستعار

ITQAN:v1p226/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p226/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p226/r4.claim: The stop after “to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy” is complete if the following divine name is nominative, and good if genitive.
ITQAN:v1p226/r4.anchor: ونحو ﴿ إلى صراط العزيز الحميد ﴾ تام على قراءة من رفع الاسم الكريم بعدها حسن على قراءة من خفض

ITQAN:v3p121/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p121/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p121/r8.claim: An original metaphor uses a borrowed generic noun, as in rope, darkness and light, or valley.
ITQAN:v3p121/r8.anchor: أصلية وهي ما كان اللفظ المستعار فيها اسم جنس

DAMGHANI:v1p309/r10.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p309/r10.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p309/r10.claim: Darkness and light can denote disbelief and faith: God brings believers out of the darkness of shirk into the light of faith.
DAMGHANI:v1p309/r10.anchor: الظلمات والنور والايمان والشرك قوله سبحانه في سورة البقرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p97/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p97/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p97/r4.anchor: والثاني : الأمر . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

NASHR:v1p226/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p226/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p226/r5.claim: A stop may be complete on one reading but only adequate on another: he contrasts the case of khāʾ in wa-ttakhidhū and the following divine name after ṣirāṭ al-ʿazīz al-ḥamīd.
NASHR:v1p226/r5.anchor: مثابة للناس وأمنا تام على قراءة من كسر خاء واتخذوا وكافيا على قراءة من فتحها

BURHAN:v2p88/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p88/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p88/r8.claim: The Qur’an is the Prophet’s enduring miracle, making the study of its inimitability especially important; revelation guides people from darkness into light.
BURHAN:v2p88/r8.anchor: وهو علم جليل عظيم القدر لأن نبوة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم معجزتها الباقية القرآن وهو يوجب الاهتمام بمعرفة الإعجاز
